articleTitle: Green synthesis of Conductive Porous Film and its Application on Screen-Printed Electrodes Used For Biomedical Application
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Currently, most researchers are choosing screen-printed electrodes (SPEs) as detectors in developing biosensors. The production of these SPEs entails thin film deposition, which entails the application of nanomaterials and binders onto diverse, flexible substrates like plastic, paper, or textiles. Nanomaterials, such as nanoparticles (NPs), nanofibers, and nanowires, improve the performance of these biosensors. Moreover, their large surface areas make them valuable for achieving enhanced biomolecule immobilization. Nanomaterial-based SPEs facilitate rapid, effortless, cost-effective on-site analysis that is exceedingly precise, replicable, and responsive. Conventional nanomaterial production methods, such as physical and chemical processes, pose hazards to human health and the environment due to harmful ingredients and unsafe reaction circumstances. A practical approach to addressing this problem is organic synthesis, called "green synthesis." Green synthesis is founded on creating and employing methods that reduce or eliminate the use of hazardous substances and waste. This article introduces an innovative method for creating a conductive porous film (CPF) using natural materials. The film created is also applied to a flexible paper-based SPE, and its electrical properties were analyzed.

articleTitle: An Improved YOLOv8 Model for Traffic Sign Detection and Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Intelligent transportation systems are aimed at improving the safety of roads and traffic management, making traffic sign detection a critical part of the system. In this work, we evaluated and compared two popular object detection models YOLOv8 and ResNet50 for the purpose of traffic sign recognition. The models were trained and assessed in various epochs to evaluate their performance. Our experiments show that the performance of YOLOv8 outperforms at epoch 47. The YOLOv8 model is characterized by an impressive accuracy of 98.32% as it presents precision, recall and F1-score values at 0.9345, 0.9428, and 0.9322, respectively. These metrics indicate that the model has a strong capability to detect and classify traffic signs based on high accuracy in field settings. On the contrary, the ResNet50 model performs worse with an accuracy of 84.32% and a loss level of 0.9932. It should be noted that this comparison is favourable as normally inter-rater reliability sits more while intra rate mostly varies upwards according to sources which have provided extensive information regarding diversity in the data. The lower accuracy and higher loss show that, in the traffic sign detection scenario, the YOLOv8 model is superior to ResNet50. Detailed evaluation of the performance models highlights that YOLOv8 possesses more effectiveness for accurate and reliable traffic sign detection, which could be implemented in intelligent transportation systems.

articleTitle: Video Captioning using LSTM-based Encoder-Decoder Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: This paper provides a way to improve video captioning by integrating the feature extraction capabilities of the VGG-16 Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) based Encoder-Decoder model. The suggested approach seeks to produce subtitles for videos that are both logical and pertinent to the context. Comprehensive visual features are retrieved from video frames by utilizing the VGG-16 model, which results in a comprehensive representation of visual content. Following the feeding of these features into an LSTM-based Encoder-Decoder architecture, the encoder processes the data while the decoder produces captions that provide context. The model can collect both spatial and temporal information thanks to the synergy between VGG-16 and LSTM, producing captions that are more visually appealing and contextually accurate. The outcome of the experiments shows how well this method works in generating high-quality video captions and how it can improve upon the state-of-the-art in video interpretation. This approach has potential for use in applications that need in-depth, complex video analysis.

articleTitle: Brain Tumour Disease Detection in MRI Images using Xception Model
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: The main aim of this study is to examine the utilization of the Xception transfer learning model for the crucial task of detecting brain tumor diseases in medical images, with a specific focus on improving mortality rates. This study highlights the urgent requirement for automated and precise techniques for detecting brain tumors in medical imaging. The present study proposed a novel Xception model architecture to classify brain tumor illness images into two categories. The study included a dataset consisting of 253 photos. The model completed training for a total of 40 epochs, employing a batch size of 8 and utilizing the default learning rate. The model training procedure involves optimizing it using a combination of Adam and Adamax optimizers. The findings illustrate the model's competence, achieving a noteworthy level of accuracy at 96%. The results of this discoveries are of considerable importance, as they demonstrate the potential of the Xception model in furthering the field of medical diagnostics. The attainment of a high level of accuracy implies enhanced capabilities in the early diagnosis and prompt intervention of brain tumor disorders, potentially leading to significant consequences for patient outcomes and healthcare practices.

articleTitle: Speaker Verification: A Raw Waveform Approach for Text Independent using CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Recognizing the speaker’s voice is the goal of speaker recognition. In general, speaker identification and verification fall under speaker recognition. Numerous deep learning-based architectures for speaker recognition have been suggested, as evidenced by the literature. The accuracy of recognition models has significantly improved with the use of i- vector or x-vector feature extraction models, yet, the architecture appears to be very complex. A scalable speaker recognition system requires lightweight models with adequate accuracy to be implemented for various security applications. The suggested framework goes in this direction by utilizing Convolutional Neural Network architecture, which is trained and tested on Libri speech data which includes short utterances of 7000 speakers. The suggested framework is trained by extracting MFCC characteristics from the provided utterance. Comparing the architecture to other cutting-edge methods, it appears to be lightweight with reasonable accuracy.

articleTitle: Tri-Band Slotted Monopole Antenna for Vehicular Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: This paper presents a compact wideband antenna specifically designed for vehicular applications within the sub-6 GHz 5G network band, encompassing a frequency range from 1.71 GHz to 5 GHz. The design incorporates a rectangular patch with a stepped structure, featuring two symmetrically raised monopoles on an FR4 dielectric material substrate. To enhance passive isolation without increasing the spatial gap between elements, a partial ground plane structure is integrated beneath the radiating patch. This configuration maintains a low-profile design while ensuring robust electrical performance across the entire frequency spectrum, consequently improving impedance bandwidth. With its compact form, broad bandwidth, and enhanced radiation characteristics, the antenna emerges as a practical choice for wireless communication devices operating within the 1.71 to 5 GHz frequency bands.

articleTitle: Optimization Of Fast Charging System For Electric Bicycle
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: The growing demand for an eco-friendly, efficient and fun type of urban transportation has made an increase in the popularity of electric bicycles (e-bike). The popularity of e-bikes has been increasing due to growing awareness of nature and the use of eco-friendly products. However, these e-bikes have a major problem with charging time. To address this problem, the project seeks to find a method for a fast charger with an efficient design and cooling system with appropriate safety features in an existing charger while being budget-friendly. The primary goal is to significantly reduce the charging time while maintaining the safety and longevity of the battery of the e-bike and also doing a comparative analysis on the existing chargers. The charger's design involves the selection of various suitable components based on the requirement of the charger such as high capacity transformer, efficient control circuits, cooling circuits, efficient converters, robust safety features and other charging circuits. Simultaneously searching for the necessary adjustments for the battery's Battery Management System (BMS). The key aspect of this project is to find the most efficient fast charging method to create an efficient and safe fast charging system for an electric bicycle. This abstract provides an overview of the various methods developed for the creation of a fast charging system while emphasizing the importance of safety and efficiency. The final product aims to provide e-bike users with a fast and dependable charging solution, enhancing the convenience and utility of this increasingly popular sustainable urban transport mode.

articleTitle: Sign Language Detection Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: In our digital age, communication should be accessible for everyone. Communication is a fundamental human right, yet millions of individuals who use sign language face daily challenges in expressing themselves and understanding others. Sign Language Detection and Text Conversion will help to break down the walls that make communication difficult for sign language users. This paper presents an innovative solution for this problem where we used MobileNetV2, Resnet50 and EfficientNet-B0 algorithm on a Kaggle dataset containing American Sign Language (ASL). We were able to achieve 98.96% accuracy using EfficientNet-B0, 98.33% accuracy with RestNet50 and 98.12% for MobileNetV2. Models were trained using 55,680 images, 13,920 images were used for validation and 17,400 images for testing purpose. TensorFlow framework is implemented for MobileNetV2, ResNet50, and EfficientNet-B0. The network consists of several layers like global average pooling, dense layer with 128 units, ReLU activation function with 29 units and a softmax with 5 epochs. Importantly, we convert these gestures into alphabets, making communication more reachable.

articleTitle: Developing Smart HyperSpectral Imaging Technology to Aid Healthcare Professionals in Sustainable Medical Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: This paper explores the potential of the rising hyperspectral imaging era to help resource healthcare professionals in sustainable clinical environments. Hyperspectral Imaging (HSI) systems can remodel regular pictures into more distinct ones with heightened analyze-capability. The generation combines virtual imaging era and chemical analysis strategies and is used to investigate and identify materials from a distance. HSI may be used to accumulate information from sufferers that would now not be available thru the traditional imaging era, enabling quicker analysis with stepped-forward accuracy. Similarly, HSI can be employed to monitor and enhance medical assets' excellence, including scientific gadgets, treatments, and environmental factors. This era can facilitate advanced affected person care while working in sustainable clinical environments. HSI may be used to minimize medical fees, lessen wasteful practices, and streamline care shipping.Furthermore, HSI can assist healthcare specialists in ensuring patient privacy and protection in these sustainable clinical environments. The information gathered from HSI can offer insight into clinical methods, remedies, and sources to assist healthcare professionals in their paintings. The application of HSI holds super capability for the healthcare region and should be further explored to understand better its capacity uses..

articleTitle: Trend Intelligent Tutoring System 2018-2022 : Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: ITS is a method of teaching that uses technology to give lessons without the need for an instructor to be there. A systematic literature review (SLR) was conducted in this research to identify the components of an intelligent tutoring system, and the results are presented. The method used in this literature review is the prism method. The steps in the prism method are slr protocol, search for literature, select literature, summarize evidence and disseminate results. The slr protocol stage, it consists of determining a research question, searching for scientific reference sources with the keyword intelligent tutoring system, then sorting out the appropriate articles and making final conclusions. This article gives a detailed look at how the intelligent tutoring system changed over time during the pandemic epoch. Our contribution is complete information on the components of ITS in times of epidemic at universities, with the goal of improving their learning and practical use of the technology.

articleTitle: Pothole Detection Using a Self Driving Car
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: With the growing popularity of self-driving cars on roads, the assurance of security and functionality is an urgent need. In that respect, detecting potholes is an important piece of research, because they are hazards not only for vehicles being driven autonomously but also those being steered by humans. This paper proposes a novel way for detecting potholes with its hardware setup including an Arduino and a Raspberry Pi, where the Arduino acts as a Slave device and Raspberry Pi acts as a Master device. Furthermore, we use the TinyYOLOv4 which is a state-of-the-art object detection model for training a large scale pothole detection dataset..

articleTitle: Utilizing Keras Model for Dynamic Drawing Analysis in Predicting Parkinson’s Disease through Spiral and Wave Patterns
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Identifying concrete cues associated with specific health issues is critical to developing effective clinical decision support systems. For patients with Parkinson’s disease (PD), the severity of the disease has been found to be directly reflected in impaired handwriting. In addition, individuals with PD exhibit decreased movement and pen pressure displayed during writing or drawing. Accurate detection of these symptoms at the onset of disease improves clinical diagnosis. This paper proposes a framework for analyzing spiral and wave patterns in PD patients and healthy subjects. The system uses the Keras model to estimate drawing patterns and uses ensemble classification based on group results to predict the probability of spiral and wave sketches. This model is trained on patient data, the model has 93.4 % accuracy overall, 94% average recall, 93.5% average accuracy, obtaining an f1 score of 93.94%.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Cooperative NOMA System with Diversity Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: The ever-evolving landscape of wireless communication demands continuous advancements in signal processing techniques to enhance reliability and performance. It conducts a comprehensive comparison between two prominent diversity combining techniques: Equal Gain Combining (EGC) and Selection Combining (SC). These techniques play a crucial role in mitigating the adverse effects of fading and signal attenuation, thereby enhancing the overall communication link quality.It begins with in-depth exploration of the fundamental principles behind EGC and SC, highlighting their respective strengths and limitations. EGC, a simple and computationally efficient method, assigns equal weights to all received signals. On the other hand, SC selects the signal with the highest instantaneous received power, providing a more selective approach. The comparative analysis encompasses key performance metrics such as diversity gain, outage probability, and bit error rate, shedding light on the trade-offs inherent in each technique.In the dynamic realm of wireless communications, the quest for robust and efficient signal processing methods is perpetual. This paper delves into a meticulous examination and comparison of two pivotal diversity combining techniques: Equal Gain Combining (EGC) and Selection Combining (SC).

articleTitle: A Performance and Power Comparison of Contemporary GPGPU Architectures
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: General-purpose Graphics Processing Units (GP-GPUs) have been extensively studied over the last fifteen years. GP-GPUs execute general purpose applications on a graphics processing instead of the traditional graphics applications. GP-GPUs employ a single instruction multiple thread (SIMT) execution wherein there are multiple processors and thousands of light-weight threads. In this article we compare the performance and power consumption of a variety of graphics processors. Specifically we compare Fermi, Kepler, Pascal, Turing, and Volta graphics processors. These are processors that were released from more than a decade back (Fermi) to the most recent processors (Volta). We observe that for a good number of applications Volta gives the best performance. Surprisingly, for few applications Pascal gives the best performance. We root-cause the reason for such a behavior and observe that the memory-level-parallelism (MLP) is the reason with Pascal reporting a higher MLP than Volta. We also observe that the power consumption mirrors the performance with identical behavior. We conclude that the performance of a GPU has many variables and only moving to a newer generation of GPU architecture will not always give the best performance.

Author Keywords: General Purpose Graphics Processing Unitsraphics Processing Units

articleTitle: Levenberg-Marquardt Neural Network-based Unit Vector Template PWM Control Strategy for Current Harmonics Mitigation in Grid-Tied Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: A control technique is proposed to mitigate the unbalanced nonlinear load current harmonics in a grid-tied photovoltaic (PV) system. The approach leverages a unit vector template generator (UVTG) and the Levenberg-Marquardt neural network (LM-NN) algorithm is utilized to improve the power quality of the system after being subjected to the disturbances caused by the load and provide grid synchronization. In this work, the neural network model was created and trained using preprocessed data through the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm. The LM-NN model is configured with multiple hidden layers and neuron topologies, which allows it to identify complex patterns in the data and generate accurate predictions. The outcomes demonstrate that the UVTG and LM-NN control strategy can reduce harmonic distortion in nonlinear loads, improving power quality and grid stability. The proposed control technique is designed and simulated using MATLAB/SIMULINK environment.

articleTitle: Fuzzy based Particle Swarm Optimization Scheduling in Cloud Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Cloud computing technology is advancing at a rapid pace. These days, the majority of industries use this technology to improve service quality, one of the biggest issues. In order to execute, the system must be able to operate efficiently with little downtime and without lowering customer expectations. Study over here elaborates the use of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm with Fuzzy Logic (FL) to replace the conventional Genetic Algorithm (GA) for task scheduling in cloud computing environment. The work collects a bunch of scheduled tasks and evaluating each task quality based on user assumptions. This work ilterates the scheduling order genetic operations for generating optimal task schedule. When every fitness function parameters are same, it takes a long time for general GA to determine the correct scheduling order. Because it considers all possible aspects of the issue, it is a built-in technique for solving problems. When used in combination with FL and PSO. It solves problems from existing database memory in the same way that the human brain does. The present scheme gives a comparison of GA, GA with FL, and GA with FL, PSO. In comparison to GA and GAFL(Genetic Algorithm with Fuzzy Logic), the suggested system demonstrated better task progress using FL and PSO.

articleTitle: Breast Cancer Prediction by Ensembling Machine Learning Algorithms and Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: A primary cause of death is cancer, which is a result of abnormal cell growth. Globally, breast cancer is a significant contributor to female fatalities, and its prevention is challenging due to unidentified causes. However, early detection is pivotal for reducing risk and improving survival rates. Advanced imaging techniques like mammography and ultrasound are instrumental in diagnosing breast cancer. This model integrates machine learning and Explainable AI to predict breast cancer. Trained on a dataset with diverse features from fine needle aspiration of breast masses, the model not only determines whether a patient is positive or negative but also sheds light on the importance of specific features of the cancerous cell. In cases of a positive diagnosis, early detection empowers patients to promptly seek essential treatment, significantly enhancing their chances of survival.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Approach for Prediction of Binding Affinity for Anti Malerial Drugs and Their Target Proteins
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Malaria, a severe illness caused by a specific parasite and transmitted through mosquito bites, poses a significant threat to life. Considerable research has been conducted in diagnosing this disease. Various drugs have been developed to combat it, notably chloroquine derivatives and artemisinin. However, chloroquine's effectiveness against the malaria parasite has been limited due to the parasite's development of resistance to the drug. Although the exact method by which chloroquine eliminates the parasite remains unclear, this research conducts a thorough investigation into the mechanism of action of chloroquine. It aims to understand how substances akin to chloroquine attach themselves to its target proteins. Furthermore, the effectiveness of chloroquine derivatives is demonstrated in this study through the binding energy exhibited by the drug towards specific proteins by introducing a novel approach for determining the drug's binding energy, using convolutional neural networks. The model ended up by giving a mean squared error of 1.23 with an R2 score of 0.65. The model has been validated with the quercetin derivatives and their target protein called pfLDH (lactate dehydrogenase proteins). The paper highlights that there are patterns in the sequences of drugs and target which can helps in leading out to the prediction of binding affinities without the use of any docking study.

articleTitle: Multi-task Convolutional Neural Network Approach for Automatic Alzheimer Disease Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: While CNN-based Alzheimer’s disease (AD) classification has showed some encouraging results, it will need high accuracy, fast processing time, and generalizability to a number of population types before it can be used in clinical settings. The brain disorder known as Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is progressive and currently has no cure. Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is characterized by a decline in memory and other mental abilities as well as a loss of autonomy in daily life. The results of this study suggest that using statistical learning and ensemble learning strategies, an image feature extraction technique like the Auto color correlogram Filter methods may be used successfully to an Alzheimer’s photos dataset. Dementia caused by Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a progressive form of the neurodegenerative brain disorder. It’s not always obvious at first since there are usually so few symptoms at the outset, and they might be similar to those of other disorders. Distinguishing Alzheimer’s disease from mild cognitive deterioration, which may be appreciated in normal aging, may be challenging.

articleTitle: A Deep Neural Network to Decipher EEG Signals and Identify the Person’s Imagined Motor Activity
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) has great potential for deciphering the motor activity of the human brain, especially when imagining an individual performing a specific motor task. This ability to interpret EEG signals and determine imaginary motor activity has important implications for the development of brain-computer interfaces (BCI) and advances in neurorehabilitation techniques. In this work, we investigate the application of deep neural networks, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), to analyze EEG signals [2] in an image-like format and classify the corresponding motor activity. The dataset consists of EEG recordings collected from subjects performing various motor tasks or motor imagery. We use preprocessing techniques to remove noise and artifacts and then segment the EEG signal into smaller epochs. These epochs are transformed into an image-like representation suitable for CNN input. Data augmentation is applied to increase the size and diversity of the data set, ensuring robust network training. CNN architectures are designed to capture spatial patterns and hierarchical features present in EEG signals. The network is trained using a suitable loss function and optimization algorithm. Performance evaluation is performed against a separate validation set using metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score [4]. This result demonstrates the effectiveness of the CNN-based approach in interpreting EEG signals and classifying imaginary motor activity. The results will contribute to the development of more accurate and efficient BCIs, advances in neurorehabilitation, and advances in our understanding of motor representations in the brain.

articleTitle: Microwave Imaging System using UWB Archimedean Spiral Antenna for Skin Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Microwave imaging (MI) has gathered the interest of cancer researchers due to its inherent advantages of being non-invasive and non-ionizing. Thus, this paper describes designing and developing a compact Archimedean-Spiral microstrip-patch antenna (ASMPA) as a sensor for skin cancer detection via a low-cost monostatic radar-based Microwave imaging (MRMI) approach. The proposed ASMPA consists of a single spiral-shaped patch fed using a slotted microstrip feed line. The designed ASMPA sensor is imprinted on a single layer of Rogers RT5880 substrate, with overall dimensions of 38×38×0.87 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The proposed ASMPA is intended to operate in the frequency range from 2.2 to 13.9 GHz (in air) with a fractional bandwidth of 145 %. The proposed ASMPA offers a peak gain of 6.8 dB at a 7.8 GHz frequency. In-silico simulation of the proposed ASMPA in the presence of a four-layered bio-phantom has been conducted in a computer simulation technology (CST) microwave studio (MWS). The Proposed MRMI procedure uses a Coherent Factor Delay Multiply and Sum (CF-DMAS) algorithm to reconstruct the image of the scanned area under test. The ASMPA design also maintains human safety by keeping a Specific Absorption Rate below 1.6 W/Kg i.e. 0.028 W/Kg at 5 GHz. This aligns with the safety criteria established by the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to minimize potential health hazards associated with exposure to radiofrequency (RF) and microwave (MW) radiation.

articleTitle: Fine-tuned EfficientNet and MobileNetV2 Models for Intel Images Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: This study looks at using two types of deep learning models, MobileNetV2 and EfficientNet, for sorting pictures in Intel's image collections. The study looks at how well it works by testing with different numbers for learning rate; these are 0.01 and 0.09 faster than the last ones, seen as goals to reach success high in speed needed fast. The study is about checking how good the models' guesses are since it shows how well they work. The MobileNetV2 model did very well, reaching the best accuracy of 99.67% at point 50 in training sessions. Instead, the EfficientNet showed a very good accuracy of 92.11% at the same time period. The side-by-side look shows that MobileNetV2 does better than EfficientNet in image sorting jobs, winning in this special situation. Changing the learning rate helps us understand how sensitive our models are to fine-tuning. This can help make training smoother and better. The results show how important it is to choose the right model and adjust its settings to get better accuracy when classifying images. This could have many uses in different areas, like seeing what objects are shown on images or finding out patterns from them.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study Between Class-Dependent and Class-Independent Algorithms of Linear Discriminant Analysis: A case study- Face Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Face recognition is the process of identifying an individual by analyzing their facial features. It has become an essential area of research due to its numerous practical applications, such as security systems, access control, and surveillance. One of the challenges in face recognition is dealing with high-dimensional data, as facial images typically contain a large number of pixels. To address this issue, dimensionality reduction techniques such as Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) can be used. In face recognition, LDA can be used to extract discriminative features from facial images and reduce the dimensionality of the feature space, thereby improving the recognition system’s performance. This proposed study aims to conduct a comparative study between class-dependent and class-independent algorithms of LDA for face recognition. both algorithms were applied to the ORL dataset containing 400 images within 40 classes and compared the results were by applying SVM as a classification model.

articleTitle: Development of Wireless Serial Server Module for the Remote operation of various Serial Field Device in ITER-India
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Serial communication finds widespread usage in industrial control systems due to its immense benefits including simplicity, reliability, and interoperability. Traditionally, the RS232 and RS485 networks have become the standard for connecting various devices and equipment for serial communication. On the otherside, wireless networks are making its way for use in industrial control system applications. The installation of wireless networks naturally provides a reduction in cable and its maintenance related costs, provides increased flexibility and mobility to enhance the performance of industrial control system. In this context, the prototype of serial wireless server module has been designed and developed successfully to operate industrial field devices with inbuilt RS232 port over Wi-Fi network. Primarily, this module converts serial data in RS232 network in Wi-Fi IEEE 802.11n format and vice versa using TCP communication. The serial wireless module is configured as a TCP server. The remote computer(PC), configured as TCP client, connects to this Wi-Fi network and remote serial device can be accessed using software application in PC. This module has multiple advantages such as completely wireless, portable, independent of auxiliary device, USB operated, plug-n-play and of easy to deploy type. The multiple modules, connected to different field devices, can be connected in one Wi-Fi subnet and accessed from single PC for control & data acquisition purpose.This paper presents the design, development and deployment of this module in detail. This module is currently installed in Pfeiffer Vacuum Gauge Controller (TPG 256A) along with custom developed windows application in PC. This application displays current pressure gauge values, saves pressure values in SQL database, can export data to Excel sheet, can configure threshold set points for digital alarm generation and act on the devices such as gate valve etc.

articleTitle: Multilingual Depression Detection in Online Social Media Across Eight Indian Languages
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Depression, a prevalent mental health concern, manifests itself on social media, providing opportunities for early detection. This study aims to fill the gap in research for low-resource Indian languages by proposing a comprehensive approach to depression detection across eight languages. By utilizing the Long Short-Term Memory and the Gated Recurrent Unit models, we provide an ensemble model that improves overall performance. Our translation-based dataset solves data restrictions related to language. Drawing insights from various studies, the literature review delves into the complexities of analyzing mental health on social media. We translate these insights into practical applications through model implementation and preprocessing techniques. The LSTM and GRU models, enriched with pretrained FastText embeddings, demonstrate competitive accuracy. The ensemble model, amalgamating their outputs, exhibits robustness in depression detection. Nevertheless, certain limitations persist, including concerns related to dataset representativeness and the nuances of informal social media language. Our study concludes with a roadmap for future research, emphasizing the need to expand datasets, develop language-specific models, and explore advanced architectures. This research contributes to a nuanced understanding of depression detection in linguistically and culturally diverse contexts, building upon insights gained from the literature review and model implementations across various Indian languages.

articleTitle: Advance Genome Disorder Prediction Model Using Deep Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: A comparative analysis of deep learning techniques for the prediction of genetic disease - cystic fibrosis. Cystic fibrosis (CF) is a complex genetic disorder that needs early and accurate diagnosis for effective treatment. To achieve this, we introduce a powerful genome disorder prediction model that uses advanced deep learning techniques. Our model is built on two key algorithms: Residual Neural Network (ResNet) and Extreme Learning Machine (ELM). We collected a comprehensive dataset that includes genetic data, clinical records, and information about the environment. Our goal was to improve the accuracy of CF prediction. After extensive testing and cross-validation, our research shows that our model performs better than traditional methods. This study is a significant step toward improving the diagnosis and personalized management of cystic fibrosis

articleTitle: Dermatoscopic Image Analysis using Fine-Tuned ResNet50: Classifying Benign & Malignant Skin Lesions
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Dermatological examinations have to rapidly detect skin lesions to improve patient outcomes and care. A refined ResNet50 transfer learning model classifies skin lesions as benign or malignant (cancers) in this study. A properly curated dataset of 3297 accurately labelled dermatoscopic pictures is used to test deep learning methods in dermatology. The dataset has three parts: 64% for training, 16% for validation, and 20% for testing. Partitioning facilitated model training, fine-tuning, and evaluation. The ResNet50 model was extensively trained on 2109 images. A separate selection of 528 pictures was used to evaluate and verify the model. This strategy maximised performance and minimised overfitting. A selection of 660 images that accurately showed a variety of real-life settings was used to evaluate the model. ResNet50, noted for its capacity to extract detailed visual information, was fine-tuned to reliably categorise skin lesions. The model accurately classified benign and malignant tumours with 93.33% accuracy. High accuracy indicates the model's great and dependable performance. Performance was measured beyond precision. These measurements included using accuracy and loss charts during training and a confusion matrix during testing. The thorough evaluation enabled the calculation of various performance metrics, demonstrating the model's dependability and efficacy in dermatologists' diagnostic processes. This paper examines the dermatology applications of deep learning (DL) models, notably the fine-tuned ResNet50 model. The model's 93.33% accuracy shows its ability to improve diagnostic accuracy. This could greatly improve clinical practises and benefit patients and healthcare systems.

articleTitle: Estimating Commercial Fish Crop Potential Using Hyper Spectral Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Fish cultivation is a critical part of global meal safety, supplying an environmentally sustainable aid of animal protein and other nutrients to tens of millions of people. The control of fish populations in aquaculture calls for effective land use planning and the most appropriate harvest to ensure that the greatest viable amount of fish may be produced within the maximum sustainable way feasible. Remote sensing gear which includes hyper spectral evaluation can offer guidance for aquaculture land use-making plans, as well as assist in estimating the capability of industrial fish vegetation in a certain area. This paper discusses the capacity of hyperspectral evaluation to degree the fraction of photo synthetically active flowers (FPAR) to be able to better understand the capability of fish manufacturing in an area, in addition to other useful packages of this generation. The implications of understanding the biophysical properties of aquatic flora for aquatic useful resource management also are discussed.

articleTitle: A Child Psychoanalysis Robot and Method Based on Behavioral Psychology
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: The use of robots in psychoanalysis has been a topic of discussion for many years. The development of children's psychoanalysis robot based on behavioral psychology may be an innovative method to treat children with mental health problems. This method will involve using a robot that is programmed to interact with children and help them express their emotions through play therapy. The core idea of this article is to propose a concept for monitoring children's mental health based on their use of learning robots. Children's psychoanalytic robots are based on behavioral psychology and its methods. The main goal of this robot is to help children learn basic knowledge of human behavior, which is necessary for their development and growth as healthy individuals. This is achieved through the use of different games, which can help them perform better in certain situations or with certain people, thereby helping them develop social and emotional skills in the early stages. A child psychological analysis robot based on behavioral psychology uses electronic learning and entertainment devices to analyze the specific behavior of children, monitor changes in their psychological state, and conduct behavioral psychological analysis, in order to detect, remind, and treat children as early as possible, and maximize the protection of their mental health. The robot will be designed to respond to children's behavior and provide feedback based on principles of behavioral psychology. This method can help children develop coping mechanisms and improve their emotional regulation skills. In addition, using robots can reduce the sense of shame associated with seeking mental health treatment, as some children may be more willing to open up to non human entities. However, it is important to note that this method should not replace traditional treatment methods, but rather serve as an additional tool for therapists. Further research is needed to determine the effectiveness of this method and ensure that it does not have any negative impact on children's mental health.

articleTitle: Investigation of 8×10Gbps WDM System Incorporating Fiber-FSO link
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: As the high data traffic is on peak and several users are approaching unlimited online information. In this paper, an 8×10Gbps wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) system using integrated fiber and free space optics link is reported and investigated. Results indicate that faithful fiber range of 50km can be obtained successfully at fixed FSO range of 10km. Moreover FSO range can be extended till 50km with constant 10km fiber link. Moreover, the comparative analysis of the realized work with other ones indicates its superiority in terms of throughput, range and capacity.

articleTitle: Enhancing COVID-19 Detection with YOLOv5 Object Detection Algorithm in Chest X-ray Images
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: In the ongoing fight against COVID-19, accurate diagnostic tools are crucial. This study focuses on the detection of COVID-19, primarily by analyzing Chest X-ray images to identify and understand the disease. We introduce a new approach that utilizes the YOLOv5 (You Only Look Once) object detection algorithm. YOLOv5 is known for its ability to quickly identify objects, and we have fine-tuned it to perform effectively with X-ray images. The result is a model that excels at identifying intricate COVID-19-related patterns in X-ray images, achieving a high accuracy score of 98%. By carefully adjusting and training the model with specific data, our method achieves even higher accuracy. This modification makes YOLOv5 a powerful tool for automating the detection of COVID-19, offering hope for early detection and timely action in the ongoing global fight against the pandemic.

Author Keywords: Object detection algorithm and Automated diagnosis

articleTitle: Fuzzy-based Induction Motor Fault Diagnosis Decision-Making System for Motor Current Signature Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Motor Current Signature Analysis (MCSA) is a leading approach for detecting induction motor faults such as eccentricity, stator, and rotor issues. This paper explores integrating Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and Wavelet Transform (WT) into MCSA to identify irregularities in current signals and provide fault information. While FFT offers faster analysis, its fault insights are limited. To address this, a time-efficient MCSA method with fuzzy logic decision-making is introduced, evaluating motor load and comparing time domain current signals to a healthy motor baseline. The method yields three outputs: Normal, FFT, and WT, optimizing fault analysis based on specific motor conditions. Validation in MATLAB/SIMULATION demonstrates improved runtime without compromising accuracy, offering a promising real-time monitoring solution for industrial induction motors, balancing accuracy and computational speed.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Saturated Medical Body Area Network using Priority Reassignment
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: IEEE 802.15.6 standard defines the Physical and Medium Access Control layers for Medical Body Area Networks (MBAN), where many sensor nodes can communicate with a central hub using a wireless medium. The standard specifies the user priorities and contention window range for the sensor nodes to enable them to achieve the best throughput and high reliability. However, there are eight distinct priority levels (UP0-UP7) which may be assigned to a maximum of sixty-four nodes, resulting in multiple nodes being assigned the same user priority. In such cases local priority needs to be assigned to the nodes within the UP and data throughput must be optimized. In this work, we have used Criteria Importance Through the Intercriteria Correlation (CRITIC) where nodes are put in a priority queue by assigning them local user priority within one of the eight priority levels UP0 to UP7, as defined in IEEE 802.15.6. The method optimizes the backoff count value to minimize the delay for data packets from these nodes in the queue. We have done simulations where results show that the backoff values and the local priorities calculated using CRITIC based upon sensor parameters – packet size, packet generation rate, and data transmission rate improve the throughput of sensors in UP0-UP6.

articleTitle: Integrated Crop Protection Management
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Addressing the challenges posed by unpredictable climate conditions and pest infestations, this proposal seeks to develop a software solution designed to aid farmers in detecting plant diseases and identifying pests. The primary objective is to empower farmers with a tool that facilitates early detection, enabling informed decision-making in crop management. By leveraging machine learning algorithms and advanced image recognition techniques, the proposed software aims to provide accurate identification of pests and diseases. This technological intervention is poised to contribute significantly to reducing crop losses and minimizing the reliance on chemical inputs in agriculture. The envisioned software serves as a valuable resource for farmers globally, offering a practical means to enhance their ability to respond effectively to emerging threats in crop health. Through this innovation, the agricultural community can benefit from a more sustainable and resilient approach to farming practices, promoting long-term viability and productivity in the face of environmental challenges.

articleTitle: Optimal Bidding Scheme Selection Algorithm based on Big Data
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: The traditional bidding scheme selection algorithm needs to construct an attribute matrix and an intuitive fuzzy linear evaluation model when selecting the optimal bidding scheme, but the model does not take into account the time problem in the process of big data processing, resulting in poor accuracy and low efficiency of the obtained results. In the highly competitive business environment, it is very important for an enterprise to choose a suitable bidding scheme for winning the bid successfully. In this paper, an algorithm for selecting the optimal bidding scheme based on big data analysis is proposed

articleTitle: SDN-based Mobile Edge Computing with Vacation of Virtual Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: A vast array of IoT devices have been implemented worldwide as cloud computing and virtualization have become more and more commonplace. Because of this, processing of computationally demanding tasks is moved from the edge to the centralised cloud, increasing energy consumption in cloud data centres and causing a noticeable delay for vital applications. The paradigm for cloud computing has shifted in recent years from centralised to mobile edge computing (MEC), where computational workloads are delegated to edge servers close to user equipment (UE). This epitome results in minimal latency for UE, effective resource utilisation at the edge, and decreased energy consumption in cloud data centres. Given this, developing optimal energy-saving solutions for resource allocation and computing job offloading in MEC networks has become a challenging challenge due to the rapidly growing size and complexity of these networks. The vacation policy is a suggested power-saving traffic management strategy for edge servers. Software-defined network (SDN) architecture allows virtual machines (VMs) to take vacations. The goal of QoS optimisation is to decrease the active servers serving the tasks while maintaining QoS criteria. Numerous performance metrics of the system are calculated, including average system size, sojourn duration, percentage of client requests fulfilled, and frequency of desertion. Lastly, many numerical results are given to demonstrate the influence of certain particular factors on the MEC performance metrics.

articleTitle: House Price Prediction Using Linear and Lasso Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: This research paper aims to predict house prices with more efficiency and accuracy. The research paper involves three machine learning algorithms, "linear regression, lasso regression, and ridge regression," that are applied to the data set of Bangalore and have various information about different places in Bangalore, like BHK, number of bathrooms, area, etc. The house price prediction is quite a difficult task, as predicting the price of the house involves many factors like area, number of bathrooms, climate condition, age of the property, and many other factors. To make predictions according to all the factors, the author has applied three algorithms, one by one. From these machine learning algorithms, we have developed a model that helps predict the prices of houses with more accuracy and a lower error percentage. This model can be very useful for both buyers and sellers, as it can justify the price of the house for both of them.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: DoConnect: Patients Health Care Application
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: In recent years, the healthcare sector has witnessed transformative changes through the integration of cutting-edge information technology. This study introduces “DoConnect,” an innovative web application meticulously crafted with Java Servlets, JSP, HTML, and CSS. DoConnect serves as a comprehensive platform, facilitating seamless patient-doctor interaction by simplifying appointment scheduling, prescription management, and medication delivery. The platform, designed to be user-friendly, employs Java Servlets and JSP to efficiently manage appointments, enabling patients to select convenient time slots and fostering secure communication with healthcare providers. Notably, DoConnect streamlines medication delivery, dispatching prescriptions directly to patients' doorsteps, enhancing convenience and operational efficiency. The integration of a judicious rating system allows patients to provide feedback, fostering transparency and accountability in the healthcare community. HTML and CSS contribute to an aesthetically pleasing and intuitive user interface, ensuring a positive user experience. This research paper meticulously details DoConnect’s architecture, design principles, and implementation intricacies, highlighting the crucial role of technological interventions in bridging the gap between patients and doctors. DoConnect exemplifies a paradigmatic application of Java-based technologies in healthcare, showcasing the potential for elevated patient care through inventive digital solutions.

articleTitle: Leaf Recognition for Classifying Plant Species using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Plants are the primary source of food derived. They are found abundantly on earth; hence their classification is critical to take advantage of the resource in an efficient manner. To find out the species to which they belong, to classify them whether they are edible, non-edible, poisonous, etc. Plant classification not only helps us in medical, research fields, etc. In our research, we have included 99 species, which we classify. This classification is done based on the spectral features, shapes, venation, edges, color, leaf pattern, and geometric features of the leaves. There are many Neural Networks used for these kinds of classifications. We in our piece of research have used Convolution Neural Network. Many other models like PNN, SVM, and KNN can also be used individually or collectively.

articleTitle: Enhancing Performance of SiGe/InAs Junctionless TFET
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: This article investigates how to optimize device performance by strategically utilizing semiconductor energy levels and gate dielectric properties. The primary objective is to optimize Silicon-Germanium (SiGe) / Indium Arsenide (InAs) Junctionless Tunnel Field-Effect Transistors (TFETs) by strategically improving their functionality. The process intends to optimize the design of junctionless TFETs for improved functionality, as they represent promising candidates for the next generation of low- power electronic devices. In the pursuit of controlling tunneling properties, the structure initiates a comprehensive investigation into band gap engineering within the SiGe channel. The optimized device’s on-state current while maintaining the desired subthreshold swing characteristics through meticulous adjustments to the band gap profile. The analysis strikes a balance between tunneling efficiency and gate control over the channel by carefully selecting and fine-tuning the gate dielectric properties.

articleTitle: Grid Collection Algorithm and its Application in Power Flow Optimization of Low-Voltage Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: In today's rapid development of high technology, the use of scientific and technological means to make the development of low-voltage distribution network better has made a trend, in order to more adapt to today's development, create a smart low-voltage distribution network, so that the automation level of low-voltage distribution network is improved, and low- voltage distribution network follows. In order to improve the stability, reliability and economy of the system,

articleTitle: Exploring the Benefits of Interactive Communication Media Algorithms for Networking Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Interactive communication media algorithms are useful tools for creating efficient and effective networking applications. Such algorithms enable the application to accurately predict user behaviour and preferences, use natural language processing to automate conversations, and integrate with other systems. This paper investigates the benefits of using interactive communication media algorithms for developing networking applications, including improved user experience, scalability, and quicker response times. Additionally, this paper will address potential limitations, such as the need for significant data collection and availability of relevant computing resources. Finally, this paper will conclude with a discussion of the potential implications of further investigations into interactive communication media algorithms for networking applications.

articleTitle: Enhance Performance of the Grid connected Induction Motor under Unbalanced Voltage Sags with ANN based Floating DC Link Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: This manuscript presents the modelling of a floating DC link capacitor as a series compensator for operating a grid-connected induction motor. The converters can produce high-frequency harmonics when the conventional three-phase H-bridge converter is used for voltage sag compensation. It can lead to electromagnetic interference (EMI) during switching action. EMI mitigation measures, such as filters, may be required to comply with regulatory standards. The proposed converter topology avoids this problem and the additional requirement of energy storage elements, transformers and power filters to mitigate the unbalanced voltage sags. An advanced artificial neural network (ANN) is developed for effective floating converter circuit switching operation. The following energy-minimized compensation (EMC) regulated floating DC link converter that is operated floating capacitors in charging and discharging modes. The ANN-based floating DC link converter maintained induction motor torque and speed at constant and obtained optimum THD in grid currents. The proposed series compensation topology has better ride-through capability against unbalanced voltage sags in grid voltage.

articleTitle: Dental Fluorosis Analysis: A Web-Based Dental Fluorosis Severity Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: The success of deep learning algorithms in biomedical applications is notable, yet their application to dental hard tissue conditions, including Dental Caries, Dental Abrasion, Dental Attrition, Erosive Tooth Wear (ETW), and Fluorosis, remains underexplored, particularly in analyzing photographic images. Traditional visual examination methods for clinical diagnostics are hindered by subjectivity. With the advancement of computer technology, there is growing interest in leveraging Artificial Intelligence (AI) for dental health. Our study in Vijayawada revealed a lack of oral health awareness among residents. Collaborating with Dr. Sandhya, we identified a significant issue—dental fluorosis affects nearly 45% of residents, with many cases going undiagnosed. Early detection and intervention could potentially reduce severity by up to 70%. This paper introduces a comprehensive solution for analyzing dental fluorosis. Utilizing Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and You Only Look Once (YOLO) architecture, our web application swiftly detects severity. The CNN model, trained on diverse data, accurately classifies severity levels, and YOLO ensures real-time analysis. Users, including patients and dental professionals, interpret severity classifications through an interactive map interface. The final classification model achieves an impressive 96% accuracy in categorizing dental fluorosis severity and an 84% precision in object detection. This convergence of advanced image detection algorithms and user-friendly interfaces marks a significant stride in advancing dental health initiatives, fostering a healthier, more informed society in Vijayawada, and beyond.

articleTitle: Enhancing Parkinson's Disease Diagnosis using Speech Analysis:A Feature Subset Selection Approach with LIME and SHAP
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a progressive neurological disorder that affects movement, posture, hand writing and speech. This disease often manifests speech related symptoms, including reduced vocal intensity, articulatory imprecision, making speech analysis a potential diagnostic tool. This paper focus on speech analysis of individuals to diagnose PD using different classifiers such as Logistic Regression (LR), Gradient Boosting classifier (GBC), Random Forest (RF), SVM, Decision Tree (DT), AdaBoost. SHAP and LIME are implemented toevaluate each feature’s significance. It’s observed that the optimal subset with 7 important features, identified with SHAP, an accuracy of 98% is attained.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Smart Learning Management System on Cloud
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: In this pioneering research endeavor, we present an advanced online learning management system meticulously crafted for hands-on hardware experiments, heralding a transformative paradigm in circuit-related education. Exploiting the potent capabilities of Internet of Things (IoT) technology, our system not only facilitates remote monitoring but also ensures secure data storage in cloud platforms, contributing a unique and impactful dimension to the educational landscape. The focal point of our innovation lies in the systematic evaluation of student performance against predefined faculty criteria, fostering an environment that is dynamic and deeply engaging.Distinguished by its provision of real-time, data-driven feedback to both students and educators, our system aspires to significantly enhance educational outcomes, marking a monumental stride in the realm of online education. This innovative approach empowers students with practical learning experiences, making a noteworthy contribution to the field of hardware experiment assessment.Furthermore, the system’s significance transcends traditional methodologies through the seamless incorporation of IoT connectivity. This integration not only facilitates the collection of valuable data on student progress and experiment outcomes but also enriches performance assessment, fostering a learning environment that is more interactive and personalized. Students can actively engage in hands-on learning experiences remotely, liberating education from the confines of traditional classroom setups.The inherent promise of this project lies in its capacity to seamlessly amalgamate cutting-edge technology, remote accessibility, and continuous performance assessment, thereby significantly elevating the quality of circuit-related education. This initiative represents a pivotal advancement in the ever-evolving landscape of online learning, promising a future where education is not only accessible but also tailored to the diverse needs of individual learners.

articleTitle: A New Exact Reversible Full Adder for High Speed Arithmetic Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: In this paper, we present a new exact reversible full adder has a ‘quantum cost’ (QC) of 9 with total delay of 7Δ. The proposed adder herein referred to as "Exact Reversible Full Adder" (ERFA). The proposed ERFA is designed using 4-Feynman gates and 1-Fredkin gate in three different stages. The proposed ERFA has ‘2’ ancillary inputs (AIs) and ‘3’ garbage outputs (GOs). Further, to verify the functionality, the proposed ERFA is designed and validated through Verilog HDL code simulation. Also, it is compared in terms of various design metrics (DMs) against 16 reversible full adders that were reported in the current literature.

articleTitle: Zen Mentor: A Yoga Monitoring and Correction Application
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Recognizing the paramount importance of accurate yoga practice to mitigate potential injuries, recent technological strides have ushered in a new era of accessible online yoga sessions. While several applications have emerged, a notable deficiency lies in rudimentary classification system, merely categorizing postures as either right or wrong. Addressing this inadequacy, our innovative approach incorporates the advanced capabilities of the MediaPipe library. Unlike conventional applications, our method involves a comprehensive analysis, monitoring the entire sequence of steps executed by the user during their yoga practice. By delving into the intricacies of each step, our system goes beyond the binary classification, ensuring that every aspect of the asana is performed with precision and in the correct order. This meticulous monitoring not only promotes a safer practice but also enhances overall efficacy, allowing practitioners to derive maximum benefits from their yoga routines. Integral to our solution is the seamless integration of the MediaPipe library into a user-friendly mobile application. Beyond improving posture assessment accuracy, this integration significantly expands the outreach of our platform. The user-friendly interface further ensures that individuals, regardless of their expertise level, can engage with the application effortlessly. This inclusivity aligns with our broader objective of making yoga practice accessible to a diverse and extensive audience, thereby fostering a healthier and more balanced lifestyle for a multitude of individuals.

articleTitle: Exploring Spatial-Temporal Metrics in Deep Learning Cancer Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: This paper examines the use of spatial-temporal rookies for most cancer diagnostics. Deep learning is an effective tool in clinical imaging to stumble on and diagnose sicknesses in an extra accurate and automated way. The latest studies are calling for the improvement of newcomers who are extra spatially aware and can consider temporal elements. This paper will analyze a number of the present-day tactics to deep master cancer diagnostics, talk about the capacity of using spatial-temporal metrics for applications associated with cancer diagnostics, and explore how such strategies can enhance present methods of scientific imaging diagnostics for cancer. It's far expected that using spatial-temporal metrics in deep getting to know most cancers diagnostics will emerge as an essential discipline to look at and produce higher results. Its research aims to explore spatial-temporal metrics' usage in deep studying cancer diagnostics. , this observation targets to research the statistics to develop metrics that could degree the impact of temporal and spatial attributes on the accuracy of most cancers analysis. By analyzing the temporal and spatial shape of the facts contained in most cancer diagnosis versions, this research seeks to improve the model's accuracy. Similarly, this study seeks to expand a set of metrics that could measure and evaluate the efficacy of various spatial-temporal fashions while evaluating and diagnosing cancer in distinctive patient populations. The results of this research can assist in increasing the accuracy of present cancer detection strategies, leading to better results for cancer patients around the sector..

articleTitle: Pre-trained VGG16 and EfficientNetB3 for Multiclass Classification of Orange Leaf Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Identifying orange leaf disease is very important to make sure that citrus fruit farms are healthy and produce a lot of fruits. In this research, we used two different deep-learning designs called VGG19 and EfficientNetB3. We made strong models that can automatically spot problems in orange leaves without help from humans. The models were trained and checked using a carefully picked range of pictures with healthy leaves, and diseased ones caused by different illnesses like Citrus Canker, Citrus Greening and so on. The learning process needed 10 and 30 rounds to show how well the model learned as time went by. Findings show that both VGG19 and EfficientNetB3 did a good job telling the difference between healthy orange leaves and those with disease. But, our research shows that EfficientNetB3 did better than VGG19. It got the best accuracy of 97.30% at round 30. This means that the better depth and simple rules of EfficientNetB3 make it work really well for handling orange leaf disease problems. These findings show how we can use these disease-finding systems in orange groves. The good results show how helpful deep learning models, especially EfficientNetB3 are in giving tools for early disease detection that work quickly and well. The study helps us understand better about growing crops accurately and shows how important it is to pick the right deep learning designs for the best results in orange leaf disease detection.

articleTitle: Utilization of Naive Bayes Classifier for Autism Risk Assessment Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: The present work investigates the use of the Naive Bayes classifier for the purpose of autism risk assessment via the implementation of machine learning methodologies. Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a multifaceted neurodevelopmental syndrome characterised by a diverse array of symptoms, hence presenting difficulties in promptly identifying and diagnosing the illness. By using a dataset that encompasses a range of variables linked to risk factors for autism, we utilise the Naive Bayes classifier to construct a prediction model. The objective of the model is to categorise people into two distinct groups: those who are deemed to be at risk of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and those who are not considered to be at risk. The research evaluates the performance of the classifier by using variables such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. Moreover, the examination of feature significance offers valuable insights into the primary elements that contribute to the decision-making process of the classifier. The findings of this study provide a valuable contribution to the expanding field of using machine learning techniques for the evaluation of autism risk. These results present a promising tool that might be used for early intervention and assistance within clinical environments.

articleTitle: Optimizing DevOps Methodologies with the Integration of Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: This research paper aims to explore the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) techniques in DevOps practices to enhance efficiency, automation, and decision-making capabilities. The paper provides a comprehensive review of existing literature on the subject and presents a case study illustrating the practical application of AI in a real-world DevOps environment. By analyzing the benefits, challenges, and potential ethical considerations, this study seeks to provide insights into how AI can be leveraged to optimize DevOps workflows. The paper provides a comprehensive review of existing literature on the subject and presents a case study illustrating the practical application of AI in a real-world DevOps environment. By analyzing the benefits, challenges, and potential ethical considerations, this study seeks to provide insights into how AI can be leveraged to optimize DevOps workflows.

articleTitle: White Blood Cell Classification using Sequential Convolutional Neural Network Transfer Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: The classification of blood cells is essential because it gives an assay that may be used in the diagnosis of a variety of diseases. In order to get beyond the difficulty and imprecision of the conventional approaches that are based on light microscopy, The construction and testing of a deep learning system that can accurately and quickly classify different types of blood cells is the primary focus of this study. Our model achieves a remarkable overall accuracy of 99% by using a huge and diversified dataset. This is a significant milestone in the field of medical picture analysis. The sequential CNN architecture exhibits its capacity to learn complex characteristics and patterns within blood cell pictures, exceeding other methods and establishing a new benchmark for the accuracy of categorization. The efficacy of sequential CNN algorithms, as well as the future of blood cell analysis, both hold the possibility of better diagnostic precision, which will ultimately lead to improved quality of life outcomes.

articleTitle: Low-Power 8x8 S-RAM Memory Design: CADENCE-Based Simulation and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Static random access memory (SRAM) and dynamic random access memory (DRAM) are two types of memory circuits that are important for system architecture and are related to power consumption. Memory usage can be reduced, thus improving reliability, performance and overall cost. Low-power SRAM is becoming increasingly important in many VLSI chips. Therefore, it is important to have a lower power SRAM that operates at a higher speed. The aim of this project is to design and simulate an 8x8 low-power SRAM memory array using Cadence tools. Initially, different topologies of SRAMs such as 6T, 7T, 8T and 9T were designed and analyzed in read and write mode. To build an SRAM memory array, different modules such as decoders, logic amplifiers, SRAM arrays, and multiplexers need to be designed and integrated. The performance of SRAM topologies was compared taking into account parameters such as propagation delay, static power consumption, static noise and corner analysis. The topology with the best performance is then considered for the low power implementation using Sleep technique.

articleTitle: Flexible Copper Tape based ECG Electrodes
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Through conformal integration across the target surface, flexible electronics a rapidly developing field of technology—offers safe, pleasant, and non-intrusive solutions to overcome challenges in recording and monitoring various bio-signals. This has the potential to change healthcare. Polymers are frequently utilized as substrates to create flexible electrodes, particularly when those electrodes need to be biocompatible and conformally bonded to the underlying substrate. Electrodes are the most common type of flexible electronic structure among these devices that are used to record bioelectric signals. Their potential uses are numerous and include monitoring physiological signals like ECG, EEG, and EMG, developing sensors for parameters like glucose levels, pH, and lactic acid, and even electrically stimulating muscles, nerves and wounds. In the present work, aluminum thin film over PDMS and Kapton tape along with readily available copper tapes were explored for electrode development. While electrodes over PDMS developed cracks and those over Kapton tape had conformality issues, proper ECG signals were received over copper tape electrodes in combination with conventional electrodes. To determine the effectiveness of this study and any prospective benefits in the areas of flexible electronics and bioelectric signal capture, the results were also compared with those from traditional electrodes.

articleTitle: Efficiently Combining Quantum Mechanics and Algorithm Design for Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Quantum mechanics offers capability benefits for optimization due to its capability to carry out calculations in parallel, but conventional quantum algorithms for optimization have commonly relied on heuristic techniques. Latest advances in algorithm layout have led to the development of new strategies for correctly combining quantum mechanics and set of rules layout for optimization. This paper critiques those new strategies and discusses their capability for enhanced optimization performance. A number of the important thing techniques mentioned encompass quantum annealing, variation quantum Eigen solvers, and quantum walks. Those techniques offer more than a few changes-offs in terms of accuracy and computational complexity. Its miles argued that they could offer positive advantages over traditional optimization algorithms, but careful consideration of the available resources is still critical for attaining the pleasant optimization results. Notwithstanding the modern-day barriers, similarly studies into the capacity of mixing quantum mechanics and set of rules design for optimization holds great promise for the sphere.

articleTitle: Implementation of the Voice Based Control and Detection of the Currency in ATM Transaction
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Automated Teller Machines (ATMs) play a crucial role in modern banking systems. However, the user interface of traditional ATMs primarily involves a touch screen and physical buttons for interaction. To improve the ATM user experience and enhance security, we propose a novel approach that utilizes voice recognition technology for user control and currency denomination detection during transactions. Our project involves developing a software interface that employs speech recognition algorithms and machine learning models to detect user commands and currency denominations. This system is designed to be compatible with existing ATM hardware, ensuring seamless integration into current banking systems. Overall, the implementation of a voice-based control and detection system for ATMs has the potential to revolutionize the ATM experience for users and increase security in the ATM environment.

articleTitle: Optimizing Bidirectional EV Charger with Rapid Charging Architecture using Fuzzy Logic Control
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: The increase in the number of Electric Vehicles (EVs) has sparked an interest in determining whether or not they can function well as energy storage devices when used in the context of microgrids. The objective of this research is to explore the use of parked EVs for efficient surplus energy storage employing bidirectional charging technology using Fuzzy Logic Control(FLC) for charger’s performance analysis.
