In order to evaluate the performance of the device, this research investigates the influence of different thickness levels. The SCAPS-1D tool is used for conducting device simulations, and a suggested device architecture consisting of Cu/PEDOT: PSS + WO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/MAGeI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/PCBM/FTO is created. The investigation encompasses a variety of thicknesses for the MAGeI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> absorber, spanning from 10 to 300 nm. The analysis of device performance optimization demonstrates that a thickness of 400 nm results in enhanced PV characteristics. These parameters include a short-circuit current density (J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SC</inf>) of 31.18 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, an open-circuit voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OC</inf>) of 0.72 V, a fill factor (FF) of 76.72%, and a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 17.42%. The aforementioned discoveries provide significant insights that may contribute to the growth of PV devices, hence enhancing the performance of tin-based devices.

articleTitle: Hybrid Curvilinear Defected Microstrip Structure to Reduce the Electromagnetic Coupling in PCB
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to mitigating electromagnetic coupling in high-speed printed circuit boards (PCBs) using a Hybrid Curvilinear (H-C) design strategy. The microstrip circuit board substrate employed is FR4, and the study encompasses a frequency range spanning 0.1 GHz to 10 GHz. By incorporating H and C shapes into the microstrip structures, the proposed methodology achieves significant reductions in both forward and backward electromagnetic coupling. Specifically, the forward coupling is reduced by an impressive -32.12 dB, and the backward coupling is mitigated by -19.16 dB. Comparative analysis against existing methodologies reveals that the H-C design approach yields superior results, showcasing its effectiveness in enhancing electromagnetic compatibility in high-speed PCB applications.

articleTitle: Remote Monitoring of Hazardous Environment at Mining Sites Using LoRa Network
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Mining sites are considered one of the most dangerous work environments due to the presence of hazardous gases. Workers are always at risk of being exposed to toxic and explosive gases such as methane (CH4) and carbon monoxide (CO). Therefore, it is crucial to monitor these gases and other environmental parameters like temperature and humidity in real-time to prevent any potential risks to human life and the environment. Although generic IoT networks are very much capable of monitoring hazardous gases from a mining site but, given the harsh environment of a mining site and being always at remote areas, a stable internet connection cannot be expected. In this study we will be making use of LoRa network, which is a wireless technology that has gained popularity in the field of remote monitoring in the recent years. LoRa operates on a low-power, wide-area network that allows data transmission over long distances without the requirement of internet. This makes it ideal for mining sites where the distance between the control room and the mineshaft can be several kilometers. We will be discussing the implementation of one sensing node to be installed in the vicinity of the mining site and would be responsible for sensing all the information and transmitting the same securely using its integrated LoRa module, and one central node which will be installed in the control room, which will be responsible for receiving the data transmitted by the sensing node, analyzing it, displaying it and generating alert if any value seems to be rising or falling into a hazardous level.

articleTitle: Intelligent Identification Method of Segmented Line Loss of Low-Voltage Power Grid Based on Ant Colony Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: The intelligent identification method plays a very important role in the identification of segmented line loss in low-voltage power grid, but there is a problem that the identification results are inaccurate. The traditional line loss identification method cannot solve the problem of intelligent identification method of segmented line loss identification of low-voltage power grid, and the recognition rate is low. In modern power system management, accurate identification and location of line losses in low-voltage distribution network has always been a key challenge to improve energy efficiency and reduce operating costs.

Author Keywords: Segmented line loss of low-voltage power grid

articleTitle: Deployment of Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) Models for Network Reliability Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: This paper discusses the deployment of Seasonal Autoregressive, including shifting common (SARIMA) fashions to expect the reliability of networks. SARIMA is an extension of autoregressive incorporated shifting average models, which seize seasonality inside the information and comprise consequences of earlier lags. The SARIMA model can be implemented to install reliability facts to expect future traits in network reliability. This paper offers an in-depth description of the additives of the SARIMA version and a step-by-step process to deploy the model for network reliability prediction efficiently. The effectiveness of this model in expecting networks’ reliability is proven by using it to present an archive of reliability records from benchmark networks. Effects display that the SARIMA version can appropriately expect the fast-time period reliability of the networks.Additionally, the paper discusses ways to leverage version estimates to design or improve destiny networks. Every day, the SARIMA version can play a vital role in consulting and decision-making associated with destiny networks’ reliability. The deployment of Seasonal Autoregressive has been studied significantly in recent years. SARIMA models are proper for predicting brief-time period adjustments in network reliability as they provide a powerful way to version seasonality traits. They’re capable of capturing the predictable periodic cycles of community occasions that occur during a specific time Of the year and the overall traits that recur each year.Furthermore, SARIMA fashions allow for the integration of autocorrelation structure of the information, that’s vital for predicting reliability trends over long durations of time. In realistic packages, SARIMA models had been used to predict traffic parameters, including the number of packets in step with 2d, packet put off, and jitter, in addition to the success or failure of packet transmissions. For instance, via predicting the modifications in packet transmission achievement/failure quotes for the duration of holidays, visitor scheduling algorithms can be stepped forward to deal with seasonal adjustments. Additionally, by monitoring the impact of upkeep and protection sports on the community’s overall performance, SARIMA models can estimate device availability for the duration of predictable operational changes..

articleTitle: NLP based Resume Analysis and Adaptive Skill Assessment System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: The proposed work introduces an innovative recruitment approach integrating LinkedIn web scraping to compile a comprehensive dataset of job descriptions and essential skills. Utilizing a pioneering Word2Vec-driven machine learning model, it efficiently categorizes job descriptions, transforming hiring practices. Job seekers benefit from a dedicated platform offering concise resume summaries and a tailored algorithm for precise role matching. Automation and personalization converge to craft custom interview questions, bridging the recruiter-job seeker gap. The goal is to enhance hiring efficiency, optimize career opportunities and talent acquisition. Performance metrics validate the model's accuracy and effectiveness in job title predictions, ensuring informed decisions for both recruiters and job seekers.

articleTitle: Search Engine for QnA using Distributed Inverted Index System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: The internet along with its global uses has also evolved as a platform where various people can pose their questions on certain sites and get them answered by others from the same domain. Certain sites like Quora, Reddit, Yahoo Answers, etc. are sites enabling people to enhance their range over the net to find solutions to various issues or answers to various questions. But this leads to redundancy in data & hence increased memory consumption where different users can pose the same question in different ways. The same thing stands for the answers posted by different users for the same question in various ways. In this paper, we have worked on a search engine system for Question & Answers where given a question, we can find similar questions with the same semantic meaning using Elastic Search which uses an inverted index system & looks at various aspects of the formulated problem statement.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Breast Cancer Detection by Mammograms
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: The most prevalent illness among women is breast cancer. The number of cases of breast cancer is rising daily and is increasing. To help the radiologist with the task of interpreting the digital mammography image to detect abnormalities related to breast cancer, an automation system utilizing an AI algorithm is proposed. Mammogram images have little contrast, but by using a trained CNN template, the medical visual quality of the image can be improved, helping with early detection. Additionally, a user-friendly Matlab-based (GUI) is created, allowing radiologists to store patient data and output images on their computers for later use.

articleTitle: Malaria Disease Detection using Convolutional Neural Network Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: This study aimed to produce a computerized identification system for diagnosing malaria disease using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models. This endeavor is aligns with the goals of the Sustainable Development that are associated with health and well-being. Inspired by recent research highlighting the potential of CNN in medical image analysis, our proposed CNN design successfully categorized photos of malaria disease into two distinct groups. This significant achievement has made notable contributions towards the progress of economical and easily accessible healthcare. The model underwent thorough training for 20 epochs with a dataset of 43,390 photos. As a result of this extensive training, the model achieved a notable accuracy rate of 94%. This technological improvement aligns with promoting innovation and infrastructure for sustainable development. The implications of the study's findings are significant for global health, as they demonstrate the CNN model's ability to analyze complex patterns effectively. This ability has the potential to assist in the timely identification and management of medical conditions, consequently making a valuable contribution towards the goals of poverty elimination and the reduction of inequalities. Moreover, by addressing health disparities, these advancements can have a positive impact on societal well-being. This study highlights the significance of technology in promoting the progress of healthcare, thereby contributing to the broader objectives of sustainable development.

articleTitle: Student Engagement and Student Outcomes: Key Findings from Based on GA-BP-ANN Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: More openness and accountability from the higher education industry is being demanded, in part, because people are worried about how well universities are using their budgets to improve student learning. There is a dearth of information regarding how financial aid affects students’ performance in the classroom. The purpose of this research was to look at how several variables, such as student engagement and certain self-reported learning outcomes, relate to educational spending. College Board and Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS) institutional data were combined with student responses from the 2014 National Survey of Student Engagement (NSSE) to accomplish this. Institutional and student variables were also accounted for in the system. During the preprocessing, feature selection, and model training phases, there is an absolute no-break condition. One part of data preparation is checking for missing values; another part is encoding and normalizing the data. After the relative features were developed, the proposed approach used the random forest method’s feature selection to find out what qualities separate students who didn’t finish the course from those who did. Training a GA-BP-ANN model requires feature extraction. With the data that is already accessible, the suggested approach outperforms the current best practices. An improvement in accuracy of 96.41% was achieved by the results.

articleTitle: Image Inpainting for Facial Recognition using Generative Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Face recognition algorithms are complicated by the presence of a face mask that obscures the majority of facial features. People wear face masks for a variety of reasons; some wear them to shield themselves from pollution, while others wear them to disguise their feelings. Masks are worn by criminals to conceal themselves from surveillance cameras and other devices. Owing to the COVID-19 pandemic, masks have become a necessity. Many Machine Learning approaches have been implemented for image inpainting and object removal. Through this study, few of the available Generative Adversarial Networks are reviewed. Further these architectures are compared and the ones suitable for removing masks from the face and regenerating the masked portion of the face have been listed. GANs are essentially computational structures that involve two neural networks against one another to generate new, synthetic examples of data that can be mistaken for real data. In this paper an analysis of four different GAN architectures have been presented. These architectures have been broadly used in image inpainting. These architectures can be used to unmask the masked faces by inpainting the portion of the face with a mask.

articleTitle: Utilising Sentiment Analysis To Predict Market Movements In Currency Exchange Rates
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: One of the most important parts of the international economy is the foreign currency market, which shows how different countries’ economies are doing. Due to the Internet’s growing popularity, more individuals are opting to articulate their thoughts and viewpoints online. Hence, we anticipate that the fluctuations in the currency exchange market will be mirrored in the textual remarks shared on the Internet. This article presents a hybrid model that integrates sentiment analysis to predict future trends in the currency market. The sentiment analysis module integrates Word2vec and Long Short-Term Memory to enhance the model’s performance and extract "emotion" variables from the text input. The algorithm utilizes sentiment analysis to identify the emotions expressed in "exchange rate" posts on "Weibo" as either "positive," "ordinary," or "negative." It then assigns an emotional weight to each day based on these categorizations. This enables the model to ascertain the emotional significance of each day. The model generates a word vector once the data-cleaning process is finished. Next, the historical exchange rate data spanning three to four years was randomly combined with the emotional weights from roughly three months to undertake mixed training, which included CNN and LSTM models. The dataset that is being used for this analysis includes information regarding the United States dollar, the Japanese yen, the euro (EUR), and the Australian dollar in relation to the RMB exchange rate, with samples spanning three to four years. As measured by metrics such as R2_Score, Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), and Mean Absolute Error (MAE), the experimental results show that the method presented in this study is better than other traditional models. Our technique predicts the Australian dollar/RMB exchange rate trend better than competing models by 38.41% in MAE, 34.42% in MSE, 3.08% in MAPE, and R2_Score. This shows our method’s average difference from the models. The average score of 6.21%, which is higher than the comparative models, indicates a significant level of resilience. After extracting the recommended method from the "emotional analysis" module, we compared our results to see how well our emotional weights for future exchange rate forecasts worked. The findings demonstrated that the module integrating "emotional analysis" exhibited significantly superior performance compared to the module lacking this component.

articleTitle: A Framework for Fully Automated Panoramic Image Stitching
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Merging photographs from multiple views to create a single panorama is termed Image Stitching. The challenges associated with image stitching encompass issues such as parallax and scene motion, photographs corrupted by noise, managing a vast number of images, and handling high-resolution images. Eliminating noticeable seams is another complex task. Computer-based image stitching is the most prevalent method, involving specialized software that identifies overlapping areas and merges them. Achieving a final image without discernible seams necessitates precise overlaps and consistent exposures. Even if two images are captured in quick succession, differences in lighting can lead to visible seams in the stitched image. The relevance of these seams varies based on the application. In this paper, an automated feature-based approach to image stitching is proposed to create a seamless and expansive panorama. Image feature extraction is done using the Scale-Invariant Feature Transform (SIFT), while feature matching is done using the K-nearest neighbor algorithm. The Random Sample Consensus (RANSAC) algorithm is utilized to calculate homographs for image warping, and a weighted matrix is used for image blending for a smooth panorama creation process. The performance of the proposed method is gauged by comparing the final panorama to an anticipated reference image and calculating the percentage image similarity, which involves the ratio between detected matches and key points.

articleTitle: Skin Disease Classification using Pre-Trained Convolution Neural Network with Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Skin disease diagnosis is critical for prompt intervention, effective treatment, public health management, and general well-being of people affected by dermatological disorders. Skin disease detection is a challenging task while classifying those diseases based on the images of common symptoms such as blisters- like rashes, skin lesions, pimples like papules & reddened skin is further more complex. The objective of this paper is to illustrate the effectiveness of transfer learning and application of the pre-trained models originally designed for the Imagenet Dataset in the context of detecting and categorizing various skin diseases. The aim of the model is to differentiate among monkeypox, measles, chickenpox and normal skin. The proposed framework utilizes the convolutional and pooling layers of ResNet50, DenseNet121, EfficientNetB5 and Xception which are pretrained models used for feature extraction. It incorporates a newly designed fully connected (FC) layer along with an output layer for the purpose of image classification. The proposed model is based on Monkeypox Skin Images Dataset (MSID) created at Islamic University in Bangladesh. The proposed framework exhibits that Xception achieved the best result among all the four pre-trained networks with 98.39% as training accuracy, 96.46% as validation accuracy and 95.80% as testing accuracy.

articleTitle: Sentimental Analysis based on Machine Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: In an age defined by the unprecedented proliferation of online content, the ability to discern sentiments within textual data has become integral across a spectrum of applications, spanning from business intelligence to the dynamic realm of social media monitoring. This study conducts a thorough exploration of sentiment analysis methodologies, placing a primary focus on the practical application of machine learning algorithms tailored to the demands of today's generation.The research conducts a comparative analysis to evaluate the effectiveness of diverse algorithms, including support vector machines, neural networks, and ensemble methods. By exploring proposed strategies to address these challenges, the study sheds light on their implications focusing on accuracy and robustness of sentiment analysis models in the present-day landscape.A comprehensive analysis compares diverse paradigms, such as SVM & neural networks, assessing their effectiveness amidst the challenges of navigating sarcasm, decoding context-dependent sentiments, and understanding language subtleties.Twitter, as a platform, presents unique challenges for sentiment analysis, marked by the prevalence of slang and misspellings, compounded by the 140-character limitTwo predominant strategies, the approach based on knowledge and machine learning, are deployed for extracting sentiments from textual data. This research delves into the machine learning approach, specifically applied to analyse Twitter posts about electronic products such as mobiles and laptops. Focusing on sentiment analysis within a specific domain elucidates the impact of domain-specific information on sentiment classification.This study introduces a novel feature vector designed for the classification of tweets into positive and negative sentiments, offering insights into public opinions about electronic products. The utilization of a machine learning framework enhances the precision and granularity of sentiment analysis in the dynamic landscape of Twitter, allowing for a more nuanced understanding of user sentiments within the electronic products domain.However, a primary challenge faced by sentiment analysis lies in the dearth of adequately labelled data within the realm of NLP. Deep learning models stand out because of their inherent capacity for automatic learning.This research paper mentions recent advancements showcasing the integration of deep learning models, such as deep neural networks, convolutional neural networks, among others, aimed at resolving various challenges within sentiment analysis. This includes tasks such as classification of sentiments, addressing cross-lingual complexities, textual and visual analysis, and the examination of product reviews, among others.

articleTitle: Increasing Accuracy of Crop Production and Yield Forecasting Using Hyper Spectral Image Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Hyper Spectral up-to-date evaluation has up to date be an increasing number of vital up-to-date in precision farming for predicting crop manufacturing and yield forecasting. The era offers an innovative and green way of reliably measuring the fitness of vegetation and crop production ability by providing high-resolution imaging information that allows estimates of crop biomass, vigor, and yield. This technology is mainly helpful in fast crop health assessment, with on-hand visuals that permit fast evaluation within the field. A significant gain of this generation is its capacity to date capture the spectral signature of flora appropriately and precisely, with date consideration advances in precision farming and precision agriculture. Using the technology, researchers have been up-to-date in creating specific spatial assessment maps of crop health, imparting local and nearby statistics approximately crop productiveness capacity. This information can be used up to date optimize management practices up to date increase productivity and yields.Moreover, the generation has recently become even more accurate by improving synthetic Intelligence (AI) algorithms, such as up-to-date gadgets and hyperspectral up-to-date, enhancing the era’s accuracy and usual reliability in modeling crop fitness. Hyperspectral picture analysis is an increasing number of unique techniques for forecasting crop manufacturing and yield. It involves the spectral measurements of a pattern of plants throughout the visible and up-to-date infrared (NIR) spectrum, which is then utilized to date to create a hyperspectral profile of the sample. Analysis of such profiles can reveal the updated presence of yield-figuring components, including updated water, nutrients, and up-to-date biomass. By comparing these components, predictive models of increase estimates may be created. The combination of high-resolution hyperspectral up-to-date analyses with airborne far-off sensing offers a remarkable level of temporal and spatial resolution accuracy. The aggregate of those methods has the capacity updated to provide farmers with particular actual-time insight into up-to-date crop increase and yield, which may be used up to date to develop well-timed intervention techniques. This advanced accuracy can also provide more accurate temporal and spatial yields for commodity invest updated, as up-to-date updates use these records to estimate future fees correctly. The accuracy of crop manufacturing and yield forecasts may be improved by leveraging the maximum hyperspectral picture evaluation technology and growing predictive models based on various spectral indices. Facts on crop health and future yields may be collected extra quickly and with more precision, thereby opening up new possibilities for each farmer and.

articleTitle: Stock Market Prediction Using Machine Learning - A Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: The stock market scenario currently is very volatile and prone to sudden changes. The market is in such a state due to factors like the pandemic, conflicts between nations, and the overall recession that’s been going on. Many indices worldwide are down from their all-time highs, but the market also shows signs of potential growth albeit it is very slow. In such a situation traders and investors must carefully consider their goals and the risks they’re willing to take. It is here where stock market prediction techniques could prove to be the determining factor with respect to making suitable investments. This paper’s goal is to describe and compare the various algorithms that are being used for the sole purpose of stock market predictions.

articleTitle: Next-Generation Enabling Technology in Cloud Computing: An Advantage for Businesses
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Major technical breakthroughs are changing how organizations and consumers interact with technology using Cloud computing, 5G, the Internet of Things (IoT), and Digital Twin technologies. Cloud computing offers scalable and adaptable computing resources, allowing businesses to store, process, and retrieve data from remote servers through the Internet. 5G, the next generation of mobile networks, offers high-speed connection with low latency, which is required for IoT devices to interact with one another. IoT enables the interconnection of common items, allowing huge volumes of data to be collected and analyzed. Digital Twin technology generates a virtual replica of actual assets, enabling businesses to mimic and evaluate real-world events in a virtual environment. This paper has identified the correlation between the above technologies and has set a path for future development. The implication of these three technologies will be to bring business near to the end user. Together, these four technologies provide the foundation for a new digital transformation era, allowing organizations to innovate and improve their operations in previously impossible ways.

articleTitle: LSTM based Soft-Sensor for Estimating Nitrate Concentration in Aquaponics pond
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: In the field of aquaponics, where fish and plants coexist in a symbiotic environment, closely monitoring nitrate levels in the water is crucial due to their profound impact on aquatic and plant well-being. Traditional nitrate measurement methods are often time-consuming and costly. Various approaches, including first principles, IoT-based sensors, and machine learning-based soft sensors, have been attempted to address this challenge. However, these efforts face challenges such as expensive sensors, infrequent data collection, multistage data processing using limited sensor types, and the need for regular maintenance like cleaning and calibration. Additionally, varied environmental conditions affect sensor suitability for different water environments, and even some machine learning-based soft sensors have proven inaccurate. In response, soft sensors, especially deep learning-based ones, have gained prominence in industrial applications for their adaptability and accuracy. These sensors provide real-time insights into complex processes without requiring expensive hardware. In this study, an innovative solution was introduced using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) technology, a neural network architecture in deep learning known for capturing complex temporal patterns. LSTM is well-suited for modeling and predicting nitrate concentration changes in aquaponics, trained with extensive data collected from various aquaponic ponds. Through rigorous evaluation, a remarkable MSE value of 0.00074 and an impressive R-squared score of 0.98 were achieved, holding potential for scaling up to commercial applications, benefiting aquaponics operations, supporting researchers, and enhancing sustainability and productivity in aquaponic systems.

articleTitle: A Constructive Role for Social Science in the Development of Automated Vehicles Based on LFM-BiGRU Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: This proposed system delves into the transformative realm of autonomous vehicles, a technological marvel that has captivated society's anticipation for its profound societal implications. While existing social science research predominantly focuses on regulatory, safety, and efficiency considerations, this method contends that these discussions fall short in comprehensively appreciating the extensive social ramifications of autonomous vehicles. Addressing this gap, the system aims to provide a more nuanced understanding of the broader societal impacts that autonomous vehicles are poised to instigate. The proposed methodology comprises three integral modules: preprocessing, feature extraction, and model training. Preprocessing involves essential tasks such as punctuation removal, URL elimination, and batch normalization. The feature extraction stage leverages TF-IDF, contributing to the discernment of significant features. For model training, the paper employs the LFM-BiGRU architecture, a distinctive aspect of the proposed method. Comparative analysis against conventional approaches, namely BiGRU-LSTM and BiLSTM, underscores the superior performance exhibited by the proposed method. This suggests that the LFM-BiGRU approach holds promise for advancing the capabilities of autonomous vehicle research and, consequently, societal understanding of this groundbreaking technology.

articleTitle: A Study on Sentiment Analysis Using Various ML/NLP Models on Historical Data of Indian Leaders
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Among the highly significant duties for any language most effective is the sentiment analysis, which is also a key area of NLP, that recently made impressive strides. There are several models and the datasets available for those tasks in popular and commonly used languages like English, Russian, and Spanish. While sentiment analysis research is performed extensively, however it is lagging behind for the regional languages having few resources such as Hindi, Marathi. Marathi is one of the languages that included in the Indian Constitution’s 8th schedule and is the third most widely spoken language in the country and primarily spoken in the Deccan region, which encompasses Maharashtra and Goa. There isn’t sufficient study on sentiment analysis methods based on Marathi text due to lack of available resources, information. Therefore, this project proposes the use of different ML/NLP models for the analysis of Marathi data from the comments below YouTube content, tweets or Instagram posts. We aim at the short and precise analysis and summary of the related data using our dataset (Dates, names, root words) and lexicons to locate exact information.

articleTitle: Hybrid CNN-Random Forest Framework for Elevated Accuracy in Powdery Mildew Disease Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: This research paper's abstract provides a thorough evaluation of the predictive capability of a model developed to classify the mango dusty leaf disease. The study uses an evaluation methodology that includes criteria like Precision, Memory, F1-Score, Support, Supported Proportion, and Accuracy and focuses on different disease Seriousness Levels. The evaluation shows the model's capacity to distinguish and categorize various disease Seriousness levels, ranging from Level 1 down to Level 10. While recall, which measures the capacity to properly recognize real positives, ranges between 92.05% and 91.43%, precision, which measures the accuracy in making optimistic predictions, goes from 93.80% to 92.29%. The F1-Score ranges from 97.62% to 99.65% and balances Precision and Recall. Additionally, the study quantifies that Support, showing the frequency of each class and providing information on the prevalence of various disease Seriousness Levels. The Support Proportion illustrates how examples differ among Seriousness Levels, which helps to explain class disparities. Precision, Recall, and F1-Score had macro-average values of 97.56%, 93.84%, and 96.35%, respectively, calculated over all classes. The weighted average measures significantly noticeably higher, displaying 95.40% for accuracy 96.00% for Remember, and 94.90% for F1-Score, while also taking class imbalances and consistency into account. The micro-average, which averages the performance over all instances, displays accuracy, recall, and F1-Score values of 96.77%, 96.49%, and 96.63% respectively. The results show how well the model categorizes the severity of mango powdery leaf disease.

articleTitle: Transforming Agro-Diagnostics: Banana Leaf Diseases Through Federated Learning CNNs
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: This paper discusses an extensive study on checking disease in banana leaves. It uses Federated Learning and Convolutional Neural Networks to find out what's wrong with them. The study uses data from five clients to examine five types of banana leaf diseases. This includes a wide variety of environmental and locational differences. The FL method, based on a federated averaging approach, helps people learn with others privately. It turns local information into a vital world model quickly and better.The central part of the study is a detailed look at how well the model works for five clients. The measures used to evaluate this include accuracy, support, and F1-score, along with precision and recall. The clients (hy_1 to hy_5) did very well. Their accuracy was always high, between 96% and 97%. The close study showed the large average was 90.41% to 93.60%, and the small average was 90.37% to 93.60%. Also, it indicated reliability in classifying diseases by giving a high level of detail with different data sources and suggesting models were very accurate for illness categorization across multiple datasets. A big part of the study involved using federated averaging to combine local data. This was important in making the worldwide model more accurate and valuable for everyone. The big, small, and weighted averages were essential to know how well the model worked. It looked at each class as they came from different places in a way that also thought about all of what we had there together. This method made sure we understood how well the model worked. It showed it could change and stay strong in different farming situations.

articleTitle: Gamified Screening For Developmental Dyslexia Among Young Readers
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: This work presents the prototype for a gamified screening tool for Developmental Dyslexia among young readers, accompanied by a suggested downstream processing of the data collected. The prototype contains visual, audio, and written task components, resulting in an engaging approach to screening for Dyslexia which factors in different aspects of the condition. The prototype has been built following an examination of the current use of Artificial Intelligence and gamification in the field to move towards a promising screening tool for Dyslexia.

articleTitle: Automatic Segmentation and Categorization of Liver Tumors in CT Scans: A Bibliometric Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Liver tumors rank as the third deadliest cancer globally and the sixth most prevalent disease worldwide. They primarily afflict individuals who frequently consume tobacco or alcohol. Approximately 75-85 percent of primary liver cancer cases are attributed to these factors. However, manually diagnosing liver tumors presents significant challenges due to tumor heterogeneity, varying shapes and sizes, imaging artifacts, and limited annotated data. The critical task of segmenting liver tumors in medical images greatly impacts diagnosis and treatment planning. Numerous techniques and frameworks have been formulated for the early identification of tumors, improving accuracy, and aiding doctors in understanding tumor characteristics such as size and volume. Nevertheless, this process is error-prone and cumbersome. To address these challenges, a proper model is needed to identify the tumor and used for real-time image processing. This paper motivates to develop a system and assists doctors in swiftly identifying and segmenting tumors from images, providing an approximation of tumor size and stage for more precise treatment. Manual diagnosis is challenging, but advanced DL methods like TransUNet help with early detection and tumor segmentation, assisting doctors in providing timely and accurate treatment.

articleTitle: Facial Expression Recognition in Video Using 3D-CNN Deep Features Discrimination
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: The focus of research work presented in this paper on improving performance in video facial expression recognition using a computationally efficient 3D convolutional neural network. An end-to-end 3D CNN method is proposed, which employs R(2+1)D Resnet18 as the backbone encoder block, followed by a spatio-temporal attention block divided into two heads for the evaluation of sparse center-loss and cross-entropy loss. The inclusion of a spatio-temporal block in the network has adaptively refined features in both the spatial and temporal domains. The network's combination of sparse center-loss and cross-entropy loss has extracted significant feature elements for enhanced discrimination in the embedding space. The proposed architecture is evaluated on three in-the-wild publicly available datasets, i.e., DFEW, AFEW and DAiSEE. On the DFEW, AFEW and DAiSEE datasets, our method required only 38.66 Giga MACs for one batch prediction and achieved accuracy of 59.28%, 59.63%, and 58.62%, respectively. The results show that, when compared to earlier works in the DFEW, AFEW and DAiSEE datasets, our method performed comparably well with significantly low computational load.

articleTitle: Predicting COPD Severity Using Machine Learning and GOLD Criteria
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Breathing problems that get worse over time are a symptom of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, or COPD. It is a catch-all phrase for a number of conditions including asthma, bronchitis, and emphysema. It is defined by a progressive constriction of the airways and an early aging of the lungs. Experts have attested to the fact that early identification helps lessen the symptoms of COPD. Thus, using GOLD criteria, patients’ COPD severity can be predicted using contemporary methods like machine learning algorithms. The proposed prediction models predict severity of COPD of the patient on a scale of 1 to 4 as prescribed by the GOLD system. Our model was trained to utilize a derived feature set and machine learning classifiers, such as SVC, Random Forest Classifier, XGBoost classifier, Naive Bayes, and Hard Voting Ensemble, with the best possible parameter choice to achieve a commendable accuracy of 97.6%. The global COPD epidemic will be lessened with the use of this method and medical professionals’ experience.

articleTitle: Robotic Navigation Unveiled:A Comprehensive Study of GMapping, Hector Slam, and Cartographer
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Robots are able to create detailed maps of their surroundings and determine their own location within them because to a technique called Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM). As the robot moves around its environment, the complex system generates and updates a map using sensor data from cameras, laser range finders, and other devices. There are several SLAM algorithms available, and they differ in terms of accuracy and processing efficiency, therefore comparisons are necessary. One of the main goals of these assessments is to identify the approach that performs optimally for a certain use case. In this work, three well-known SLAM algorithms are assessed: Hector GMapping, Cartographer, and SLAM. To make this evaluation easier, this research makes use of the Robot Operating System (ROS) in combination with RVIZ and Gazebo software. This study's main goals are to measure how long it takes the Burger robot model to navigate a new interior environment and to carefully assess the accuracy of the maps produced by each algorithm. The research's conclusions and observations provide insightful advice for choosing the best SLAM algorithm for practical robotic applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Medical Image Classification Using Self-Supervised Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: the goal of medical image classification is to accurately identify and diagnose a given pathology from imaging modalities. Traditional supervised methods approach this task by labeling the imaging data in a supervised manner, which relies heavily on access to a large dataset of labeled images. This can be costly and accessible in certain scenarios. Self-supervised transfer learning seeks to tackle this deficiency by learning on large, labeled datasets from related tasks and applying those learned representations to solve the medical image classification problem. This approach has proven effective in improving performance and making the best use of limited resources. This paper reviews recent literature and techniques related to self-supervised transfer learning for medical image classification tasks, and provide an overview of the underlying principles and implications for its possible applications…

articleTitle: Cauliflower Leaf Disease: Unraveling Severity Levels with Federated Learning CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: The present research deals with a new approach to precision agriculture, particularly the classification of cauliflower leaf disease using Federated Learning (FL) integrated into Convolutional Neural Networks. The study presents a new categorization scheme for leaf diseases that uses four severity levels based on the distribution of a dataset through 4 different clients. It aimed to exploit the decentralized nature of FL to improve data privacy while benefiting from powerful image classification potentials offered by CNNs. Two of the four clients in our study, fq1 to fq4, provided local data combined via Federated Averaging into a global model. The result analysis applied three key metrics: macro, micro, and weighted averages that portray the model's local and international performance. The results from every client indicated a steady increase in classification accuracy. The Macro Average at approximately even treatment of all the classes increased steadily from fq_1 (96.35%) until fq_4 (99.11%). Similarly, the Weighted Average that considers class representation began at 96.45% for f q_1 and ended at 99.10 % table for fq_4. The same pattern was obtained with the Micro Average in which contributions from all classes are summed up to have this average increased markedly, that is, 96.44% for fq_1 and sharply rises to a total of 99.10%% it reached its peak at time f: When computing based on percentages correctly assigned, the assumption made right before Class These averages show the overall balanced performance of the model for different severity classes regardless whether they appear more often in a dataset or not.

articleTitle: Peer To Peer Confidentiality in Social Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: This research paper investigates peer-to-peer (P2P) confidentiality within social apps, addressing the need for effective and user-friendly privacy methods in today's digital age. With the increasing emphasis on peer-to-peer communication in social networking, user privacy has become critical. This research looks into many aspects of P2P confidentiality in social applications, including present issues, existing solutions, and possible developments. The research begins with a thorough investigation of the inherent privacy difficulties connected with peer-to-peer communication in social applications, emphasizing the hazards of data leakage, unwanted access, and identity disclosure. It analyzes the consequences of privacy violations in terms of user confidence and data security. Addressing these concerns, the study examines existing P2P confidentiality solutions such as end-to-end encryption, anonymous routing, and secure authentication protocols. It assess the efficacy and limitations of different methods, focusing on the trade-offs between security and usability. It also investigate user perceptions and adoption rates of various strategies. The study also looks into new technologies like blockchain-based solutions and decentralized identity systems, as well as its potential to improve P2P confidentiality in social applications. It evaluate their viability and their influence on the user experience. This research paper provides insights into the complicated landscape of P2P confidentiality in social apps, highlighting the critical necessity for robust privacy safeguards. It offers a comprehensive overview of the issues, current solutions, and future possibilities for protecting user privacy in P2P transactions, with a concentration on balancing security and usability. Understanding these characteristics allows social app developers, security experts, and policymakers to collaborate to create a safer and more privacy-respecting online environment for users.

articleTitle: DeepFungusDet: MobileNetV3 Model in Medical Imaging for Fungal Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: A fungal infection in humans is a pathological state resulting from the infiltration and proliferation of fungi within the body. Microorganisms known as fungi are present in the air, water, soil, and plants. The fungal infection can cause skin to become red and inflamed causing bad oral and genital effects in the body. The article presents a deep learning technique for identifying fungal infections using MobileNetV3, which is a compact and resilient convolutional neural network (CNN). The model is trained on a wide variety of fungal datasets, demonstrating its efficiency and mobility for real-time detection using portable devices. The model can categorize and identify various fungal infections across different conditions using its deep learning capabilities. The findings result in an excellent accuracy and speed of the model in identifying fungal infections, indicating its potential for rapid and accessible detection in healthcare, agriculture, and environmental monitoring. The work investigates the effectiveness of the MobileNetV3 model named DeepFungusDet in identifying fungal infections using a broad dataset containing various fungal infections. This model has been implemented at different numbers of epochs resulting in the highest accuracy identification of 93.14% at epoch 13 and a loss of 0.4494, indicating its promise in recognizing fungal infections. This tool provides a portable option for real-time identification via mobile devices, paving the way for future research and use in the crucial field of fungus identification. The findings represent a major step forward in fungus detection and provide prospects for developing accessible and practical diagnostic tools in the healthcare industry and related fields.

articleTitle: Adopting Knowledge Transfer to Improve Medical Image Segmentation with Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: the adoption of deep learning for scientific photograph segmentation has made remarkable advances in the biomedical field in recent years. Deep mastering-based total fashions require high volumes of annotated photos to be powerful, making records series and annotation luxurious and in-depth. An expertise switch has been proposed as an effective manner to bridge the gap between limited datasets and deep mastering version performance—these paper evaluations present literature on tactics to improve clinical photo segmentation with deep studying through understanding transfer. The methods can be categorized as pre-training or first-class-tuning, with the previous use of off-the-shelf deep studying models and shifting understanding from non-clinical datasets to medical datasets, even as the latter trains on scientific datasets and transfers know-how from similar medical datasets. The advantages and disadvantages of each approach are discussed, as well as the demanding situations worried in expertise switch. Numerous future research instructions on knowledge switches for medical photograph segmentation with deep getting-to-know are outlined.

articleTitle: Alzheimer’s Disease Diagnosis Using Artificial Intelligence and MRI Images of the Brain
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: One major neurodegenerative disease that primarily affects the senior citizen and pre-elderly population is Alzheimer’s disease. Advances in AI-enhanced detection for Alzheimer’s disease have been spurred by recent developments in MRI technology, raising hopes for early detection and prompt therapies. This advancement has made it possible to create complicated models and algorithms that can analyse imaging data, improving the efficiency and accuracy of diagnosis. It gives rise to hope for the groundbreaking possibilities in transforming the management of Alzheimer’s disease and more successful treatment plans and better patient outcomes. This article aims to give a thorough overview of current advancements in DL techniques used to classify different stages of Alzheimer’s disease based on brain MRI scans, with a focus on early diagnosis. It also discusses possible obstacles and future research possibilities, highlighting the shortcomings of the current research.

articleTitle: Enhanced Multiclassification of Avocado Leaf Diseases: CNN and Random Forest Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Through the use of advanced machine learning techniques, the primary objective of this research is to develop and evaluate a classification model to identify a variety of illnesses that may affect avocado leaves. Despite exhibiting remarkable accuracy, recall, and F1-score metrics, the model displays good performance across a wide range of illness categories. The accuracy levels of the model, which range from 92.61% to 95.32%, are indicative of the effectiveness of the model in reliably detecting different kinds of diseases. Furthermore, recall rates, ranging between 91.53% and 94.44%, demonstrate the model's efficacy in collecting important cases within each illness categorization. The model demonstrates resilience in the classification of avocado leaf diseases, as it maintains an overall accuracy of roughly 93.66% during its operation. These results suggest that the model has the potential to facilitate early disease diagnosis and accurate identification, which would give major contributions to the enhancement of disease control systems in avocado farming.

articleTitle: SFNet: Synergistic Fusion Network for Text Localization in Natural Scene Images
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Prior methodologies for the detection of scene text have demonstrated promising outcomes across many evaluation metrics. Nevertheless, despite the utilization of deep neural network models, their effectiveness is sometimes limited in complicated situations due to the intricate interplay of several stages and components within the pipelines, which ultimately governs overall performance. This study presents a straightforward yet robust methodology for identifying textual content in practical environments. Phrases or text lines may be predicted in images of varying orientations and quadrilateral forms using the suggested pipeline’s single neural network. This eliminates the need for superfluous intermediary steps such as candidate aggregation and word division. Due to the streamlined nature of our SFNet(Synergistic Fusion Network), our primary emphasis is directed at the development of loss functions and neural network design. The suggested approach has been evaluated using a well-established dataset including ICDAR 2015. The results of these experiments demonstrate that the new technique outperforms existing techniques in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. The proposed methodology demonstrates a performance metric, namely an F-score of 0.89 while operating at a frame rate of 13.2 frames per second and a resolution of 720p using the ICDAR 2015 dataset.

articleTitle: Classification of Network Security Attack using KNN (K-Nearest Neighbour) and Comparison of different Attacks through different Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Network security refers to the systematic measures used to safeguard computer networks and the sensitive information they transmit against potential harm, unauthorised entry, and breaches. The concept encompasses a range of strategies and protocols designed to ensure the continued accessibility, secrecy, and reliability of network resources. The technique of categorising and assigning labels to different types of detrimental actions and vulnerabilities that specifically target computer networks is sometimes referred to as network security attack categorization. The categorization discussed herein plays a vital role in the field of cybersecurity by enabling the understanding, identification, and management of security concerns. In the field of cybersecurity, a valuable strategy involves the classification of network security attacks via the use of the K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN) algorithm. Additionally, the comparison of numerous attacks may be conducted by using various machine learning methodologies. In conclusion, the categorising of network security attacks is a fundamental aspect of cybersecurity that plays a crucial role in safeguarding computer networks and the sensitive information they contain. This strategy enables organisations and security specialists to effectively analyse, identify, and mitigate a wide range of threats. In summary, the K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN) algorithm demonstrates a high level of accuracy, reaching 99.5%, when fine-tuned with various classification parameters. This result is derived from the methodology given in the present work.

articleTitle: Sugarcane Leaf Health Grading Using State-of-the-Art Deep Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: The abstract provides a thorough summary of a classification model intended to assess the health characteristics of sugarcane leaves in different classes. The precision values of the model range from 96.93% to 97.40%, which indicates its superior performance metrics and guarantees the precise identification of positive cases inside each class. The recall values show how well the model captures most real positive events while minimizing false negatives, ranging from 96.96% to 97.48%. The precision and recall of an F1-Score are well balanced, as seen by their constant hovering around 97%. A dataset with well-distributed values and percentage of support exhibits a balanced representation across classes. The model, which uses CNNs and SVMs, achieves 87.39% accuracy on 11,133 images. The model successfully classifies sugarcane leaf health with an amazing overall accuracy of 99%, demonstrating its proficiency in this area. The weighted average, micro average, and macro average measures all support the model's consistency and dependability across classes. The class-wise evaluations' unweighted mean, or the macro average, is 97.18%. The model's strong handling of different class sizes is highlighted by the weighted average, which accounts for class imbalances depending on support and is in line with the macro average of 97.19%. The global aggregate provided by the micro average for all classes is in perfect alignment with the class-specific measures, indicating the overall superiority of the model. Together, the findings establish the classification model as a potent and trustworthy instrument with excellent accuracy and precision across a range of health categories for evaluating sugarcane leaf health.

articleTitle: IOTA's Market Dynamics and Future Impacts
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: This research examines the crucial necessity for a thorough comprehension of the IOTA cryptocurrency and its market dynamics. This analysis examines the price trends and trade volume, which are essential factors for identifying patterns and correlations within the bitcoin market. This study places significant emphasis on the function of market speculators, particularly highlighting the influence of emotional trading behaviors. Furthermore, it underscores the close interdependence between IOTA and Bitcoin. Moreover, it acknowledges the relatively new advent of IOTA in the realm of cryptocurrencies, as it endeavors to gain acknowledgement. The data presented in this study add to a deeper understanding of the dynamics of bitcoin, providing valuable insights. Furthermore, the acquisition of knowledge from this study can be utilized to construct environmentally sensitive and sustainable blockchain infrastructure in developing countries, thereby meeting the crucial requirement for fair and comprehensive technological advancement.

articleTitle: An Efficient Approach to Estimating Heart Rate from Facial Videos with Accurate Region of Interest
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Contactless Heart rate measurement of the cardiac pulses provides an effective way of physical assessment during pandemic situations where physical contact is highly risky. Remote photoplethysmography (RPPG) provides the solution for contactless monitoring of blood volume pulse from facial videos. This article presents an efficient technique to estimating the heart rate from facial regions. The work mainly focuses on extracting the Region of Interest (ROI) from face images which are robust against illumination and motion changes. The work includes the skin standardization mechanism that could be able to locate the appropriate ROI irrespective of the skin tone of the subject, thereby increasing the effectiveness and application of the approach in real-time scenarios. The proposed method compares with traditional methods to assess and evaluate accuracy, consistency, and sensitivity. The proposed approach attains faster processing with a decrease in the number of elements for processing decreased by 5 times.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Single Image Deblurring
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Atraditional assignment in basic computer vision is picture deblurring, which involves recovering a clear image from a hazy input picture. Significant progress has been made in overcoming this problem thanks to developments in deep learning, and numerous deblurring networks have been proposed. To provide the community with a helpful literature review, this work provides an extensive and timely evaluation of newly released deep-learning-based image deblurring techniques. We begin by going over frequent reasons for image blur, introducing performance measurements and benchmark datasets, and then summarising various approaches to the problem. We then provide a thorough analysis and comparison of convolutional neural network (CNN) methods utilizing a taxonomy based on architecture, loss function, and application. Furthermore, we talk about a few domain-specific deblurring applications, such as text, face photos, and stereo image pairs. Finally, we address important issues and potential future research avenues.

articleTitle: An Edge Computing Framework for Data Analysis in Intelligent Transportation Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) have been identified as a key application of the Internet of Things (IoT). In order to reduce latency and bandwidth needs, edge computing offers a distributed computing architecture that can process and analyse data closer to the source. In this paper, we propose an edge computing framework for data analysis in ITS and present experimental results to evaluate its performance. The proposed framework aims to address the challenges associated with traditional data analysis techniques by leveraging the power of distributed computing resources, advanced analytics, and real-time processing capabilities. The rationale behind the framework’s design and architecture is to improve the efficiency, scalability, and adaptability of ITS solutions, ensuring faster decision-making, reduced latency, and enhanced overall transportation performance.

articleTitle: Facial Expression Embrace: A CNN-SVM Approach for Multi-Class Emotional Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: This study introduces a new CNN-SVM model that can categorize facial expressions into seven distinct emotional states: Happy, fear, angry and neutral became happy; disgust and surprise also changed to an active form. To evaluate the model in detail, we employ F1 Score (harmonic mean of precision and recall), support, and total accuracy. The model’s most impressive results are recall scores and accuracy rates indicating how effective it is at distinguishing emotions such as happiness or fear. Afraid performed well on all counts, achieving a score of 94.5 % according to the F1 Score which factors in both recall and accuracy. The wide applicability of the model to handling events within individual emotional categories is verified by its strong performance in both Happy and Anger (the two largest Support groupings). According to results with 0.97 for Happiness, 0.96 each for Fear on the one hand and Anger or Neutral moods on the other, while Disgust comes in at only three-tenths of that value, accuracy is usually very high indeed. Afraid’s 0.98 accuracy rate is remarkable, clearly setting it apart from the pack. The work has implications not only in the development of emotion recognition technology but also offers many insights into HCI and affective computing. The results made here provide a solid foundation for further progress in this field, which is somewhat obscure but has begun to make headway through the categorization of human emotions based on facial expressions.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Plant Health Management with Technological Digital Transformation to Enhance Disease Control & Fortifying Plant Resilience
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: In the face of escalating global challenges to food security, the imperative for precise, efficient, and effective plant disease identification and management has grown significantly. This study delves into digital technologies’ potential for transformative change in tackling this pressing issue. These technologies encompass a spectrum including Augmented Reality (AR), Internet of Things (IoT), 5G, Blockchain, AI, ML, and RPA. This paper integrates practical insights from various real-world case studies spanning diverse geographic locations and technological platforms. This synthesis culminates in a proposed digital process, incorporating an integrated system that harnesses the synergy of various technologies to facilitate early disease detection, accurate diagnosis, and targeted treatment, ultimately resulting in superior crop yields. The research concludes by extending the scope and envisioning future opportunities for digital technologies in agriculture. The focus is on scalability, cost-effectiveness, efficiency, and sustainable growth. This comprehensive exploration demonstrates how digital technologies have the potential to revolutionise plant disease identification and management, providing substantial advantages. This research aims to benefit policymakers, farmers, communities, and consumers by showcasing their capacity to transform agricultural practices.

articleTitle: Cardiovascular Disease Prediction using Boosting Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Heart and blood vessel illnesses are collectively referred to as cardiovascular diseases. Smoking, having high blood pressure, having high cholesterol, and being obese may all raise the chance of developing certain cardiovascular illnesses. Heart disease diagnosis is a challenging undertaking that can offer an automated assessment of the patient's heart health to enhance the efficiency of future treatment. Therefore, machine learning algorithms are required to make better decisions in the prediction of heart diseases. Boosting algorithms combine multiple weak learners to a strong learner in a sequentially manner which iteratively improves the observations. The prediction of cardiovascular disease is important since it allows for the possibility of saving lives. To enable comparisons, the results are presented separately. Based on the findings, it was concluded that the proposed model generated the maximum accuracy with XG Boost, 90%.

articleTitle: Predicting House Price Model : A Comprehensive Analysis with Random Forest and Decision Tree Method
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: This paper explores the field of predicting property prices through a thorough comparison of several regression techniques. Linear regression, decision tree regression, random forest regression, K-neighbors regression, gradient boosting regression, and XGBoost regression are the regression models that are being examined. Finding the best model to reliably estimate house prices based on a set of features is the aim.The dataset used in this study includes location, bedroom count, square footage, and other relevant parameters that are known to affect property values. Each regression model is trained and tested on this dataset using a methodical evaluation procedure, and its performance is evaluated using important metrics including R-squared, Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and overall correctness. predicting house prices mainly use harlfoxem (Owner) repository of housing dataset will contain the homes sold between May 2014 and May 2015 with 21613 entries and 21 attribute were used to evaluate the performance of machine learning prediction model. For practitioners and scholars working in real estate, housing market analysis, and related sectors, this study offers insightful information. It emphasizes how crucial it is to properly choose regression techniques depending on the particulars of the prediction task and the distinct qualities of the dataset.

articleTitle: Indian Sign Language Recognition for Hearing Impaired: A Deep Learning based approach
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: People with hearing impairment or hearing disability needs sign language for communication. A sign language in America popularly known American Sign Language (ASL), in China known as Chinese Sign Language (CSL) are being used by over 45 million people with hearing impairment to bridge the communication gap with ordinary people. Despite of that, the use of Indian Sign Language (ISL) in India is very primitive or unknown to many ordinary people. Ordinary people having very meagre knowledge over this sign language, makes it difficult to bridge the communication gap with impaired once. So, the system that recognizes sign language can help both impaired people and ordinary people in communicating with each other, not only that it can be very crucial for them in emergency situations. Because of increase increasing growth of hearing impaired this field of research has gained significant importance, moreover its wide range of application including video games, Vedic mathematics, mental and fast calculations etc. has made it more significant. This article presents a Statc Sign language recognition, which aims to detect a specific motion of hands, identify and classify them using useful Transformer Encoder tool Vision Transformers (ViT). Deep learning-based recognition models such as Transformer encoders, Pre-trained CNN models such has ResNet/VGG-16 can be used in implementation of recognition tasks.

articleTitle: Robust and Predictive Deep Neural Networks for Stock Price Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Forecasting stock prices has become a widely researched domain, and conventional prediction methods primarily rely on statistical and econometric models. Nevertheless, these methods encounter challenges when confronted with dynamic, nonstationary time series data. The advent of the internet alongside the surging prevalence of social media has brought about a significant shift. Online news snippets and user comments now frequently mirror investor sentiments and perspectives on various stocks, encompassing a wealth of crucial insights that can greatly enhance stock price prediction. In this paper, forecasting of stock prices has been implemented using two cutting-edge deep learning models, namely Long Short-Term Memory and Gated Recurrent Unit. Both models have been evaluated on two publicly available datasets, namely the Google stock price dataset and Tesla stock price dataset. Experimental results show that LSTM has achieved accuracies of 87.91% and 85.67%, while GRU has achieved accuracies of 93.62% and 88.78% on the Google dataset and Tesla dataset, respectively. Keeping in view the complexity of the dataset, the obtained results, in turn, pave the way for practical applications within the dynamic realm of real-time stock market prediction.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of Crowbar Protection Technique for Doubly Fed Induction Generator under Symmetrical Fault Condition
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: This paper investigates the protection schemes for a Doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) when subjected to a fault. A Crowbar protection technique is proposed to mitigate the effects of voltage dip on the DFIG system. Three different crowbar topologies are designed, and their impact on the DFIG system’s electrical magnitudes, such as currents, voltages, and torques is evaluated. The work demonstrates the proposed crowbar protection technique can effectively enhance the DFIG system’s low-voltage ride-through capability and reduce the stress on the rotor-side converter.

articleTitle: Unveiling the Intricacies of Cyber Harassment Intentions on Social Media Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Cyberbullying is a severe issue that impacts teens and adults alike. Errors like hopelessness and suicide have resulted from it. The demand for material on social media platforms to be regulated is growing. In the work that follows, machine learning and natural language processing are used to construct a model to identify cyberbullying in text data. The program leverages data from two different types of cyberbullying: personal attacks on Wikipedia forums and tweets containing hate speech. To determine the optimal approach, three feature extraction techniques and four classifiers are examined. The method produces more than 80% accurate data from Wikipedia and more than 90% correct data from Twitter.

articleTitle: Customer Feedback System Based On Facial Expressions
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: Customer feedback is the information from the customer about the experience of services offered by the retailer. It helps the store owner to improve the customer service. The changes in the customer feedback collection systems aim to reduce the time and complexity of submission. One such straightforward approach to a customer feedback system is the facial expression based emotion feedback collection system. The facialexpression based emotion feedback system is the magnified thought of Emotional Artificial Intelligence (EAI) and can have applications, including telerehabilitation and Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS). This paper focuses on enhancing the performance of the customer feedback system. The authors used the FER-2013 dataset to train the algorithm. VGG16 is a CNN-based architecture designed explicitly for classification and localization, and the model is trained with 7 class classifications of emotions, including Happy, Neutral, Sad, Disgusted, Surprised, Fearful, and Angry. The real-time image is captured using the Caffe Model face detector and validated using the trained emotion detection model. The web interface displays the emotion detected with corresponding ratings. The collected feedback is stored as a log file with the date, time, rating, and emotion detected once the customer presses the submit button. This convenient consumer feedback system reduces the customer's response time and helps retailers improve their services.

articleTitle: Smart Disease Detection: Unifying CNNs and Random Forests for Accurate Pear Leaf Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference for Innovation in Technology (INOCON)
abstract: The abstract summarizes their findings and presents a novel method for the automated detection and categorization of illnesses affecting pear leaves by combining Random Forest models and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). Using a carefully selected dataset of high-resolution photos, the model achieves impressive precision values, from 96.77% to 98.14%, demonstrating its capacity to reduce false positives for various disease classes, such as Leaf Spot, Powdery Mildew, Pear Rust, and Fire Blight. The model's ability to capture the majority of true positive occurrences is confirmed by the consistently high recall values, which range from 97.11% to 97.56%. This improves the diagnostic accuracy of the model. Moreover, the model's overall effectiveness is supported by the F1-Score, which is a harmonic mean of precision and recall with values ranging from 97.07% to 97.74% for various illness categories. This study evaluates the pear illness classification model using a dataset of 4746 photos. 97.34%, a remarkable total accuracy rate. The support values demonstrate this model's resilience over a large dataset, and the support proportion values underline the dataset's balance, which enhances the model's ability to generalize well. The model's overall success in disease classification is reflected in the weighted average and macro-average metrics, which offer a thorough assessment of the model's performance. The macroaverage is continuously high at 97.34%. This performance is mirrored by the weighted average, which corrects for class imbalance and validates the model's accuracy for a range of disease categories. The combined CNN and Random Forest method performed exceptionally well overall, taking into account both false positives and false negatives, as seen by the micro-average accuracy of 97.35%.
